about: The referee's settlement of DEV-01's two blind counts (judging/mechanisms.a.json and .b.json) over judging/mechanism-list.json, by REQUIREMENTS DEV-10. Written 2026-11-10. The catalogue is MECHANISMS.md.

state_vars.meaning: One group's ordered log on each replica: the committed part and the uncommitted tail. A group is whatever unit holds one log and one writer (a Raft group; an ISR partition; a loglet chain; a log of objects).
Each Raft replica's current term and the vote it gave in that term.
The point up to which a group's log is committed (Raft's commit index; ISR's high watermark; a loglet's quorum-acked end; the last answered PUT).
A Raft group's voters, its one pending change (or joint configuration) and its config epoch, the count of committed changes.
A group's non-voting replicas (learners, standbys).
Who leads a group now (the Raft leader; an ISR partition's leader; elsewhere the server that holds the writer role).
Not durable: a leader hand-over asked for or in flight in a group: its target, and the old leader's stop on new writes.
Not durable: each replica's election timer, and the leader's record of which voters it heard from within the election timeout.
Not durable: the leader's pending ReadIndex requests and the acks that confirm them.
Each replica's snapshot of a group's state at one index, and the log prefix dropped below it.
The rows of the partitions a group holds, as folded on each replica that folds.
Per group: whether it is quiet (it sends nothing while idle), and the offset it went quiet at.
Per group: whether it is dormant (its state is on disk only, a small record, loaded on wake).
Per group: a placement target and a preferred leader stored in its log by a planner hint.
Per group: which of its voters are log replicas (they vote and keep the log, never fold or serve).
Per replica: whether it stopped cleanly; under the memory rung an acknowledged tail may not be on its disk.
Per project-owned group: the settings class (copies, durability) it serves.
Not durable: the writer's log-end state, the fold of its committed state plus its uncommitted tail, against which writes are judged.
Per group, where the writer is not simply the Raft leader: which server holds the writer role, and the epoch of that role (RLOG, SLOG, OBJ).
Per group: the writer time t stamped on each batch; it never goes back.
In the metadata group, per slot of a resource: the group that holds it open or is about to, with the version of that write.
Per slot: the last sequence number stamped.
Per slot: its epoch; it rises when records of the slot may have been lost (an unfence after an abort, a recovery, a restore).
The entries of one slot move in the source's and the target's logs: exporting, importing, fenced(N), the copy and END(N), open, cancel, abort, unfenced.
The promise of one move at a time: a lease row in #meta, or the mover's one pending proposal.
Not durable: write load and size per slot, range and group, as the mover or splitter sees them.
The entries of one re-key (rk, cut, frz, cp, flip) in the old and the new groups' logs.
A project's fixed lane count and the hash that maps every (resource, partition) onto a lane.
The entries of one split (spl, init) in the parent's and the child's logs.
The entries of one merge (mrg, sub, mgd) in the two groups' logs.
Per group: the key or hash range it holds, and a generation that rises on every split or merge.
Kept for ever: for each group made by a split, its parent and the offset base at which it took over.
The session registry (#sessions): per client life, a session and the lease that keeps it.
Per group, tagged by slot: per session the outcomes at or above the client's floor, and that floor.
The session generation; a restore raises it, so retries from before the restore are refused.
Per group, tagged by slot: per issuer the highest call id seen and the committed outcomes above the floor (the dedup window).
Per (producer, partition): the producer's epoch, its last sequence and its last cached batches; and the producer ids handed out.
Per caller key, for its ttl: a claim with a lease, and the first result.
Per (consumer, source slot, output slot): the highest source sequence applied.
Per lock (#locks): its holder, its lease end and its version, which is the fence token.
Per group, carried with a moving slot: the highest token seen per lock.
Per unit (#sagas): its steps and its direction (run, undo, done, undone).
Member records in the metadata group: id, life, disk incarnation, roles, addresses, code hashes, and the state mark (live, draining, retiring, gone).
Resource records in the metadata group: name, config (slots, copies, durability, history, rules), allowed code hashes, the write gate, the generation pointer.
Per group in the metadata group: its resource, its incarnation, and its last known replicas and leader (a routing hint).
The controller's list of live commands, each naming the config epoch it was decided at.
The cluster id: in every dir's boot record, in #meta's first entry, and (where genesis is a conditional create) in the object store.
Per pair of members: whether the link is up and when it last answered, as each side sees it (the gone timer).
Each member's view of its peers' clocks, carried on pings or session heartbeats.
Not durable: a latency score per member, for the slow-leader rule.
Per member: its session with the controller and that session's epoch.
What a member has made durable of each group's entries, terms and votes (the journal, a WAL per group, an LSM tree, or log objects).
Per-group segment files cut from the journal, their indexes by offset, slot and partition, and the cut records.
Per dir: a random incarnation id written when the dir is made; a new or wiped disk gets a new one.
In the object store: uploaded old segments, snapshot layers and merged bases.
OBJ only: the manifest object that names a group's log head, snapshots and writer lease; changed by compare-and-swap.
The highest epoch ever used, recorded outside the restored data (the store's manifest).
PD only: the LSM tree's memtables, sorted files and compaction state.
Not durable: a byte budget per tenant per second in a process that pools tenants.
Held by a subscriber (a row only for a consumer): per slot the epoch and the last sequence seen, with the cluster id and the resource's incarnation.
Not durable, on a server: which subscribers follow which partitions, and their read credits.
Not durable: messages of the none rung on their way to current subscribers; they never enter the log.
Not durable: how many writes a client or link may have outstanding, and the edge's handshake budget per tick.
Not durable: writes a non-leader server holds in flight for a leader, each copy forwarded once.
In a smart client: its cached table of slot (or range, or partition) to leader.
A committed entry in each group's log that names the fold version in force from that offset.
Per process: which kernel worker (and so which journal) each group is pinned to.
Not durable: the shared-memory ring between a host's daemon and the app's Node process.
Not durable: calls in flight at a partition leader's host.
PD only: per key, its versions by commit timestamp, and the safe point below which old versions are collected.
PD only: the last timestamp the oracle handed out, and the window it saved before use.
PD only: per transaction, its primary and secondary locks on the keys it writes, and its commit record.
PD only: per group, the closed timestamp below which no new write will commit.
Not durable: the leader's read lease, a time promise that no other leader exists until it ends.
ISR only: per partition, the in-sync replica set.
ISR only: per partition, the leader epoch, and each replica's start offset of every epoch.
ISR only: per partition, the eligible leader replicas.
ISR only: per transactional id, its producer id and epoch, the transaction's state and the partitions it wrote.
ISR only: per partition, commit and abort markers and the last stable offset.
SLOG only: per loglet and log node, a sealed flag; and the recovered end of a sealed loglet.
SLOG only: per data group, the chain of its loglets with their log nodes, starts and ends.
V4 only: per author (a member's life), its own numbered log of the changes it stamped.
V4 only: per cell, the stamp of the change that holds it now (member-list version, ticket, author).
V4 only: per link, a list of the highest ticket held for each author.
V4 only: per removed cell, a deleted-at marker with its stamp.
V4 only: per (author, row), the point below which a replica has compacted its log.
V4 only: per slice, an orphan mark on a copy this replica may no longer serve.
V4 only: that a former keeper deleted its copy of a slice, or that a paused link's queue was thrown away.
V4 only: per slice being copied, the one chosen teacher and the changes held aside; per store, a latch set by a failed fsync.
V4 only: per slice copy, the staged data from the teacher and its end marker.
V4 only: per (author, row) and holder, a possession floor and a durable floor.
V4 only: per feeder and spoke, the words the feeder owes the spoke about sheds and re-latches.
V4 only: per slice, the holders that have proved they hold everything up to the crash-stable frontier.
V4 only: per row, the members that may take over stamping it.
V4 only: the member list and its version, the ballots and votes for the next view, and held members.
V4 only: for each row, the one member the ring picks to stamp its changes.
V4 only: per pending write, which holders have attested that they hold it.
BUY only: everything the bought log keeps (streams and sequences, its own consensus and metadata, its dedup window, consumers, buckets).

Per dir: the lock file with its holder's record and lease, the lease's epoch carried in the name of every file, retired-<epoch> directories, and the boot record that names the end offset a new holder reads to.
In #meta's cluster record: the planner lease, the row that keeps two planners from fighting (DESIGN-V5 4.2 and the #meta record table). Apart from move.lease, the one-move-at-a-time row.
Z par only: per entry, a mark that its checksum failed; per group, which damaged entries may be the only committed copy.
In #groups, per consumer group: a row with a lease for each member, and the group's generation.
In #meta's cluster record: the cluster version, the kernel and protocol version in force; every frame carries its sender's protocol version.
In #meta: the door secret (current and next), the CA key as envelopes to each #meta voter's key, single-use join tokens, each member's certificate, and revoked certificates.
Per message row of a queue: its claim's lease end and its delivery count; the dead-letter resource that holds rows past the limit.
In #meta, per fork: the parent's snapshots and segments that the fork's groups start from, which the parent may not drop.

Per process: the recording of every kernel input (whole frames, ticks, disk and store completions), with bulk bytes named by journal reference, and the window it must replay; the journal keeps every segment that window refers to, so the journal's truncation reads it (E-42).

mechanisms.name: Raft log
mechanisms.option: raft, rlog (and the metadata group of isr and slog)
mechanisms.state: Each replica's ordered entries of one group (index, term, payload): a committed part and an uncommitted tail.
mechanisms.rules: Only the leader appends. A follower takes entries only when the entry before them matches, and cuts a tail that conflicts (log matching).
mechanisms.model: E-14, E-14b, E-14c: TLC on etcd's own TLA+ spec; no rule count by ablation
mechanisms.source: SPACE 2 R `raft`; DESIGN-V5 4.2 'A shard is a Raft group'; Ongaro and Ousterhout 2014; etcd's raft and its port (E-10, E-46 measured)
mechanisms.precedent: a: Ongaro and Ousterhout, 'In Search of an Understandable Consensus Algorithm' (USENIX ATC 2014), section 5.3 (log replication, the Log Matching property); etcd's raft, log.go and raft.go. | b: Ongaro and Ousterhout, 'In Search of an Understandable Consensus Algorithm', USENIX ATC 2014, section 5.3; etcd's raft (log.go, raft.go)
mechanisms.why: Both counters agree. a: Same state (each replica's entries with index and term), same rules (only the leader appends; a follower checks the entry before and cuts a tail that conflicts), same role. The study ran etcd's own source and TLA+ spec (E-10, E-14). | b: Same state (each replica's entries by index and term), same rules (only the leader appends; a follower checks the entry before; a conflicting tail is cut), same role. cited from memory, sure of the system and the mechanism.

mechanisms.name: Term and vote
mechanisms.option: raft, rlog (and the metadata group of isr and slog)
mechanisms.state: Each replica's current term and the vote it gave in that term, on disk before any reply that depends on them.
mechanisms.rules: A replica votes once a term, only for a candidate whose log is at least as up to date. A candidate with a majority of its own configuration's voters leads the term; no member campaigns while a committed change is unapplied (A-01).
mechanisms.model: E-14, E-14b, E-14c: TLC on etcd's spec; the campaign guard is 1 of the 16 membership rules
mechanisms.source: SPACE 2 R `raft`; DESIGN-V5 4.2 'Who stands for election'; AMENDMENTS A-01 (the campaign guard), A-02 (jitter 0.25 E)
mechanisms.precedent: a: Raft (ATC 2014), sections 5.2 and 5.4.1 (one vote a term; the up-to-date check); etcd's raft, raft.go: hup() will not campaign 'since there are still pending configuration changes to apply' (read here, line 984 of the copy the study downloaded). | b: Raft paper sections 5.2 and 5.4.1; etcd's raft, raft.go: hup() refuses to campaign while a committed config change is unapplied
mechanisms.why: Both counters agree. a: Same state, rules and role. A-01's campaign guard is etcd's own line. The 0.25 E jitter is a constant, not a rule. | b: Same state (term and vote on disk), same rules (one vote a term, only for a log at least as up to date), same role. The campaign guard of A-01 is in etcd's code. cited from memory, sure of the system and the mechanism.

mechanisms.name: Commit index
mechanisms.option: raft, rlog (and the metadata group of isr and slog)
mechanisms.state: The highest index a majority of the group's voters hold (on disk, under `persisted`); the leader stamps it on later messages and followers learn it.
mechanisms.rules: The leader advances it when a majority of voters, itself once its own fsync lands, hold an entry of its own term. A new leader first commits an entry of its own term.
mechanisms.model: E-14, E-14b, E-14c: TLC on etcd's spec; no rule count by ablation
mechanisms.source: SPACE 2 R `raft`, Q `maj-d`; DESIGN-V5 4.2 'The commit'
mechanisms.precedent: a: Raft (ATC 2014), sections 5.3 and 5.4.2 (commit by a majority; only entries of the leader's own term); Ongaro's thesis, section 10.2.1 (the leader writes its own disk while it sends); etcd's raft, maybeCommit. | b: Raft paper sections 5.3 and 5.4.2; Ongaro's thesis section 10.2.1 (the leader writes its disk in parallel and counts itself only once its write lands); etcd's raft async storage writes
mechanisms.why: Both counters agree. a: Same state, rules and role. | b: Same state (the commit index), same rules (a majority of voters hold an entry of the leader's own term), same role. cited from memory, sure of the system and the mechanism.

mechanisms.name: Configurations and joint consensus (membership on commit)
mechanisms.option: raft, rlog (and the metadata group of isr and slog)
mechanisms.state: The group's voters, the one change that may be pending (or the joint configuration), and the config epoch: the count of committed changes.
mechanisms.rules: One change at a time, as a log entry that takes effect when it commits. Only a voter of its own applied configuration stands; a removed leader steps down; a lost disk never returns under its old id (A-01).
mechanisms.model: E-14, E-14b, E-14c (TLC on etcd's spec): 16 rules for membership in all (E-14b's 14 plus E-14c's 2); 12 of 13 non-equivalent mutants caught
mechanisms.source: SPACE 2 R `raft`; DESIGN-V5 4.2 and decision 22; AMENDMENTS A-01 (reasoned for the raft-rs rows)
mechanisms.precedent: a: Ongaro's thesis, sections 4.1 and 4.3 (one server at a time; joint consensus); etcd's raft: a change takes effect when its entry is applied (confchange package), and StepDownOnRemoval (raft.go, read here); etcd's runtime-reconfiguration guide (a member that lost its data is removed and added under a new id); TiKV's region epoch (conf_ver) for the count of changes. | b: Ongaro's thesis chapter 4 (one change at a time; joint consensus); etcd's raft confchange package, where a change takes effect when it is applied, and StepDownOnRemoval; TiKV's region epoch (conf_ver) for the count of changes; Kafka KIP-853 for 'a lost disk never returns under its old id'
mechanisms.why: Both counters agree. a: Same state and rules in the same role. A-01's five rules are in etcd's code or its guide, and were model-checked on etcd's spec (E-14, E-14b, E-14c). For the raft-rs rows the fix is reasoned (raft-rs lacks StepDownOnRemoval, E-10), but the rule added is etcd's, so it is still published. | b: Same state (voters, the one pending change, a change count), same rules, same role. Taking effect on commit is etcd's own published choice. cited from memory, sure of the system and the mechanism; KIP-853 checked on the web on 2026-11-10.

mechanisms.name: Learners (non-voting replicas)
mechanisms.state: The group's non-voting replicas: they copy the log, and fold where the row folds on replicas (in SLOG and RLOG they are the servers).
mechanisms.rules: A new replica joins as a learner and is promoted only once it has caught up. A learner grants a vote when asked and never stands (A-01).
mechanisms.model: E-14b (TLC): 'learners grant votes' is 1 of the 16 membership rules
mechanisms.source: SPACE 2 V `+lrn`, SPACE 3 R1.L; DESIGN-V5 4.2; etcd learners; AMENDMENTS A-01 (2)
mechanisms.precedent: a: Ongaro's thesis, section 4.2.1 (a new server catches up as a non-voting member first); etcd's learners (etcd v3.4 learner design; raft.go, Step: 'learners must be allowed to cast votes', read here, line 1223); CockroachDB's non-voting replicas. | b: Ongaro's thesis section 4.2.1 (non-voting members catch up first); etcd learners (v3.4 design); etcd's raft, raft.go Step: a learner answers a vote request and never campaigns
mechanisms.why: Both counters agree. a: Same state, rules and role. 'A learner grants a vote and never stands' is etcd's own comment and code. | b: Same state (non-voting replicas in the config), same rules (join as a learner, promote once caught up, grant a vote when asked), same role. cited from memory, sure of the system and the mechanism.

mechanisms.name: Snapshots
mechanisms.option: raft, rlog (and the metadata group of isr and slog)
mechanisms.state: Each replica's snapshot of the folded state at one index, and the log prefix it has dropped below it.
mechanisms.rules: A replica cuts a snapshot at a committed index and may then drop its log below it. The leader sends a snapshot to a replica that is behind its log start (InstallSnapshot).
mechanisms.source: SPACE 1 B0 (snapshots on local disk); DESIGN-V5 3.4 and 4.1; Raft's InstallSnapshot; E-46 (snapshots measured under Maelstrom)
mechanisms.precedent: a: Raft (ATC 2014), section 7 (log compaction, InstallSnapshot); etcd's raft, Storage.Snapshot and MsgSnap. | b: Raft paper section 7 (log compaction, InstallSnapshot); etcd's raft MsgSnap
mechanisms.why: Both counters agree. a: Same state, rules and role. | b: Same state (a snapshot at one index and the dropped prefix), same rules, same role. cited from memory, sure of the system and the mechanism.

mechanisms.name: PreVote and CheckQuorum
mechanisms.option: raft, rlog (and the metadata group of isr and slog)
mechanisms.state: Not durable: each replica's election timer, and the leader's record of which voters it heard from within the election timeout.
mechanisms.rules: A replica asks for pre-votes before it raises its term. A leader that has not heard from a majority steps down; the check runs every E/4, and on a quiet group it reads the link pings (A-02).
mechanisms.source: DESIGN-V5 4.2; AMENDMENTS A-02; E-38 (simulated on etcd's raft), E-38c and E-13 (measured on etcd 3.5.17)
mechanisms.precedent: a: Ongaro's thesis, section 9.6 (PreVote) and section 6.2 (a leader steps down when it has not heard from a majority for an election timeout); etcd's raft, Config.PreVote and Config.CheckQuorum (raft.go, read here). | b: Ongaro's thesis section 9.6 (PreVote); etcd's raft Config.PreVote and Config.CheckQuorum; CockroachDB's quiesced ranges, which lean on node or store liveness while a range does not tick
mechanisms.why: Both counters agree. a: Same rules in the same role. The state is not durable, so by DEV-10 (a)'s letter this is a set of rules, not a mechanism. Checking every E/4 is a constant (E-38). Reading link pings on a quiet group is the quiet-group rule, judged there. | b: It holds no durable state, so by DEV-10 (a)'s letter it is a rule set of the leadership state, not a mechanism. Its rules are published; E/4 is a constant (A-02). cited from memory, sure of the system and the mechanism.

mechanisms.name: Leader transfer
mechanisms.option: raft, rlog (and the metadata group of isr and slog)
mechanisms.state: Not durable: a transfer in flight (its target, and the leader's stop on new writes).
mechanisms.rules: The leader stops taking writes, brings the target up to its log end and sends TimeoutNow, so the target stands at once. Writes caught in the transfer are refused, never dropped (A-02).
mechanisms.source: DESIGN-V5 4.2 'A planned handover'; AMENDMENTS A-02; E-13 (measured), E-38 (simulated)
mechanisms.precedent: a: Ongaro's thesis, section 3.10 (leadership transfer, TimeoutNow); etcd's raft, MsgTransferLeader and MsgTimeoutNow; a proposal that arrives while a transfer is under way is dropped with ErrProposalDropped (raft.go, read here, line 1304), which the caller sees as a refusal. | b: Ongaro's thesis section 3.10 (leadership transfer, TimeoutNow); etcd's raft MsgTransferLeader, MsgTimeoutNow, and ErrProposalDropped for a write caught in a transfer
mechanisms.why: Both counters agree. a: Same rules in the same role. Not durable. A-02's 'refuse, never drop' is how etcd's caller already sees a dropped proposal. | b: No durable state. Same rules (stop new writes, bring the target to the log end, TimeoutNow; refuse, never drop), same role. cited from memory, sure of the system and the mechanism.

mechanisms.name: ReadIndex
mechanisms.state: Not durable: the leader's pending read requests, each with the commit index it had and the acks that confirm it still leads.
mechanisms.rules: The leader confirms with a majority that it still leads (one round, no fsync), then answers once its fold reaches that commit index. The request is the group's own message and wakes a quiet group.
mechanisms.source: SPACE 2 W `ridx`; DESIGN-V5 4.2 'Reads'; Raft thesis 6.4; E-46 (measured: linearizable in every Maelstrom run)
mechanisms.precedent: a: Ongaro's thesis, section 6.4; etcd's raft, ReadIndex with ReadOnlySafe (raft.go and read_only.go). | b: Ongaro's thesis section 6.4; etcd's raft ReadIndex (ReadOnlySafe)
mechanisms.why: Both counters agree. a: Same rules in the same role. Not durable. Linearizable in every Maelstrom run (E-46). | b: No durable state. Same rules (one round to a majority, then wait for the fold to reach that index), same role. cited from memory, sure of the system and the mechanism.

mechanisms.name: Link pings (one ping per member pair)
mechanisms.option: failure detector: one ping per member pair
mechanisms.state: Per pair of members that share a group: whether the link is up and when it last answered, as each side sees it; the pings also carry each side's clock.
mechanisms.rules: Two members of one cluster that share a group ping every ping.ms when no other frame went their way; a peer silent past evict.after is gone to this member. Past 100 members a bound on linked peers per member is needed (A-12, a placement rule).
mechanisms.source: SPACE 2 C (the failure detector sub-choice); DESIGN-V5 4.2 'Failure detection'; CockroachDB's store liveness; AMENDMENTS A-12 (E-25, E-11 measured)
mechanisms.precedent: a: CockroachDB's store liveness (pkg/kv/kvserver/storeliveness and the leader-leases design, v24.3: one heartbeat per pair of stores, shared by every range the two share), and CockroachDB's RPC heartbeat, whose answer carries the server's clock for the RemoteClockMonitor (pkg/rpc/heartbeat.proto). Cited from memory; DESIGN-V5 4.2 names store liveness too. | b: CockroachDB: pkg/rpc heartbeat (one ping per node pair; PingRequest and PingResponse carry the sender's clock, read by RemoteClockMonitor in pkg/rpc/clock_offset.go) and store liveness (pkg/kv/kvserver/storeliveness: one heartbeat per store pair, shared by every range)
mechanisms.why: Both counters agree. a: Same state (per pair: when the peer last answered, and its clock reading), same rule (ping when idle; a silent peer is gone for every group the two share), same role (one failure detector for many groups, and the clock readings the time rule needs). The peer bound past 100 members (A-12) is a placement rule with no state; its nearest published form is the scatter width of Copysets (Cidon et al., USENIX ATC 2013). It was not built here. | b: Same state (per pair: is the link up, when it last answered, the peer's clock), same rules (one ping per pair whatever the number of groups; silence means gone), same role. The peer bound past 100 members (A-12) is a placement rule with no state; its published form is the scatter width of Copysets (Cidon et al., USENIX ATC 2013). cited from memory, sure of the system and the mechanism.

mechanisms.name: Quiet groups
mechanisms.state: Per group: whether it is quiet, and the offset it went quiet at ('quiet at i').
mechanisms.rules: A leader with no writes for two ticks, whose live voters all hold its commit offset, tells them 'quiet at i' and stops sending. Any write or read index wakes it; a follower below i asks to wake; a returning link reports log ends.
mechanisms.source: DESIGN-V5 4.2 'Quiet shards'; SPACE 3 R1; AMENDMENTS A-12 (needed from phase 2); CockroachDB's quiesced ranges; for PD, TiKV's hibernate regions; E-11, E-25 (measured, no failure injected)
mechanisms.precedent: a: CockroachDB's quiesced ranges (pkg/kv/kvserver/replica_raft_quiesce.go: a leader with nothing pending, whose live followers are caught up, sends a quiesce heartbeat and stops; a lagging follower is told so it can ask to wake; any proposal or message wakes the range). For PD: TiKV's hibernate regions (tikv/rfcs, text/0023-hibernate-raft.md, read here). | b: CockroachDB's quiesced ranges (pkg/kv/kvserver/replica_raft_quiesce.go: the leader quiesces when it has nothing pending and its followers hold the commit index; any proposal or message wakes it); TiKV's hibernate regions
mechanisms.why: Both counters agree. a: Same state (per group: quiet or not, and where), same rules, same role. DESIGN-V5 4.2 copies CockroachDB's rules by name. | b: Same state (a quiet flag per group and the index it went quiet at), same rules, same role. cited from memory, sure of the system and the mechanism; TiKV's hibernate regions checked on the web on 2026-11-10 (they cut ticks and messages).

mechanisms.name: Dormant groups
mechanisms.state: Per group: a dormant mark. A dormant group is on disk only (a 24-byte record of term, vote, commit and log end; 57 B in memory) and is loaded on wake.
mechanisms.rules: A quiet, fully committed group is written to the dormant store and dropped from memory; the first message, write or open for it wakes it.
mechanisms.source: AMENDMENTS A-15 (E-36, E-26 measured; reasoned for SPLIT and SLOG); precedent on offer: TiKV's hibernate regions (cited from memory)
mechanisms.precedent: None (both counters). Nearest: TiKV's hibernate regions and CockroachDB's quiesced ranges stop a group's ticks but keep it in memory (quiet-groups' precedent); Orleans grains and Durable Objects unload idle units, which hold no Raft state.
mechanisms.why: Both counters agree. a: The precedent on offer does not match. TiKV's hibernate regions only stop the ticks: the peer stays in memory and the leader still sends slow heartbeats (tikv/rfcs 0023-hibernate-raft.md, read here). That is the precedent for quiet groups. CockroachDB builds a range's Raft group on first use but never drops it again (from memory). I searched and found no multi-Raft system that writes an idle group's term, vote and commit to a small record, drops the group from memory and loads it on the first message. Systems that do unload idle units (RavenDB databases, Orleans grains, Durable Objects) hold no Raft term or vote, so the state is not the same. Waking is a Raft restart from its saved hard state, which is published, but when a group may go dormant and what wakes it are fero's own rules, and nobody has run them with failover (K-22). Novel. | b: No precedent holds. TiKV's hibernate regions, the one on offer, only stop a region's ticks and messages (checked on the web on 2026-11-10: TiDB docs and forum); the peer stays in memory, as CockroachDB's quiesced ranges do. That is the precedent for quiet groups, not for dropping a group from memory. A web search today found no production multi-Raft system that unloads an idle group and loads it on wake. Nearest by rule but in another role: Orleans grains and Durable Objects (an idle unit is unloaded and the next message wakes it); Pulsar loads a topic only when a client opens it. So the state (a dormant mark and a 24-byte record) and the wake rule are fero's.

mechanisms.name: Slow-leader rule, the controller's form
mechanisms.option: raft, rlog with C cent or cent-co (A-03)
mechanisms.state: No durable or replicated state is named (A-03 leaves open whether this is a mechanism): a latency score per member, kept by the controller.
mechanisms.rules: The controller moves leadership away from a member that is much slower than its followers. The rule was named, not built or modelled.
mechanisms.source: AMENDMENTS A-03 (E-38 simulated, E-38c measured); precedent on offer: TiKV PD's evict-slow-store scheduler (cited from memory)
mechanisms.precedent: a: TiKV's slow score and PD's evict-slow-store-scheduler (TiDB docs, from v5.2.0: each store reports a score from 1 to 100; at 80 or more, and when only one store is slow, PD moves the leaders off it). Confirmed by search. | b: TiKV and PD: each TiKV store computes a slow score (1 to 100) and reports it; PD's evict-slow-store-scheduler evicts the leaders from the one store whose score reaches 80 (TiDB docs: slow node detection since v5.2.0, PD scheduling)
mechanisms.why: Both counters agree. a: Same state (a slowness score per member, used by the controller), same rule (the controller moves leaders off the slow member), same role. E-38 cited it from memory; it checks out. By DEV-10 (a)'s letter it has no durable or replicated state: it is one more trigger for a leader transfer. Named, not built or modelled. | b: REQUIREMENTS X17 says to count a slow-leader rule in DEV-01 and to prefer a published fix, so it is judged though it names no durable state. Same state (a slowness score per member, known to the controller), same rule (the controller moves leadership off the slow member), same role. checked on the web on 2026-11-10.

mechanisms.name: Slow-leader rule, the leader's own form
mechanisms.option: raft with C self or self+p (A-03)
mechanisms.state: No durable or replicated state is named (A-03 leaves open whether this is a mechanism): a latency score per member, kept by each leader.
mechanisms.rules: A leader that is much slower than its followers hands leadership over by itself. The rule was named, not built or modelled; no precedent is on offer for this form.
mechanisms.source: AMENDMENTS A-03 (E-38 simulated, E-38c measured); AMENDMENTS section 4 (COMP can use only this form)
mechanisms.precedent: CockroachDB's lease shedding on IO overload, read at its source on 2026-11-10 (master, pkg/kv/kvserver/allocator/allocatorimpl/allocator_scorer.go: ExistingLeaseCheck, with kv.allocator.lease_io_overload_threshold_enforcement = shed, whose default there is shed, and kv.allocator.lease_shed_io_overload_threshold, default 0.4). A leaseholder store whose own IO overload score (which adds a disk-unhealthy score) is at or above the threshold and above 1.75 times the mean of comparable stores sheds its leases to stores that are not overloaded. Each range's own leaseholder runs the check; there is no controller. PR 117703 lowered the threshold while the setting was still off by default.
mechanisms.why: Referee, with the source read. Same state: a slowness score per store, compared with the peers' mean, where the leader runs. Same rule: a leader whose own score passes a threshold and sits well above its peers' hands leadership away by itself. Same role: a slow leader in a cluster with no controller. Only the score's input differs (storage overload and disk health there; latency against the followers here). fero's rule was named, not written (A-03), so its form is still open, and REQUIREMENTS X17 asks for the published fix. So it settles as not novel on one condition: fero builds it in CockroachDB's form (an absolute threshold plus a margin over the peers' mean). b's doubt, that the feature is off by default, does not hold on the current source. By DEV-10 (a)'s letter it names no durable state; X17 asks to count it, so it stays in the file.

mechanisms.name: Member records in #meta
mechanisms.option: every row with a metadata group
mechanisms.state: Per member in the metadata group: id, life, disk incarnation, roles, addresses, code hashes, and its state mark (live, draining, retiring, gone).
mechanisms.rules: A joiner writes its own record. The metadata group's leader (or a hint) marks a member gone when its links have not reached it for evict.after, and clears the mark when that life returns. A leave marks itself retiring first.
mechanisms.source: DESIGN-V5 4.2 '#meta, the cluster's own shard', 'Healing: Members', 'Leaving'; SPACE 3 R1; for PD, ISR, SLOG and OBJ the same records in their own metadata store
mechanisms.precedent: a: Kafka KRaft's broker registration (KIP-631: RegisterBrokerRecord with the broker id, an incarnation id per start, endpoints, features, and the fenced and controlled-shutdown marks; the controller fences a broker whose heartbeats stop); CockroachDB's liveness records with their draining and decommissioning marks. | b: Kafka KRaft broker registration records (KIP-631: broker id, incarnation id, epoch, endpoints, features, fenced, in controlled shutdown); CockroachDB's node liveness records (epoch, draining, membership: active, decommissioning, decommissioned)
mechanisms.why: Both counters agree. a: Same state (a record per member in the metadata group, with a per-start id and a state mark), same rules (the joiner registers itself; the metadata leader marks a silent member; a leaver is marked first), same role. | b: Same state (one record per member in the metadata group, with its life and a state mark), same rules (a joiner registers itself; the metadata leader marks a silent member; a leaver is marked first), same role. cited from memory, sure of the system and the mechanism.

mechanisms.name: Resource catalog in #meta
mechanisms.option: every row with a metadata group
mechanisms.state: Per resource in the metadata group: name, config (slots, copies, standbys, durability, history, rules), allowed code hashes, seed applied, write gate.
mechanisms.rules: The first fero(name, opts) that creates a resource writes its record, with its first group and that group's slots. A later open that differs is refused; alter changes it online.
mechanisms.source: DESIGN-V5 4.2 '#meta' and 4.5 'Defining and changing a resource'; AMENDMENTS section 4 (COMP's table: 0 in SPACE, inside R1)
mechanisms.precedent: a: Kafka KRaft's TopicRecord, PartitionRecord and ConfigRecord (KIP-631: a create writes the topic with its first partitions; a second create is refused; AlterConfigs changes it online); CockroachDB's system.descriptor with zone configs. | b: Kafka KRaft TopicRecord, PartitionRecord and ConfigRecord in the metadata log (a topic is created on first use, a second create is refused); NATS JetStream stream configs (a create with a different config is refused); CockroachDB descriptors
mechanisms.why: Both counters agree. a: Same state (one record per resource in the metadata group), same rules, same role. The code hashes and the write gate are fields, not rules. | b: Same state (one config record per resource in the metadata group), same rules (the first create writes it; a differing open is refused; alter changes it online), same role. cited from memory, sure of the system and the mechanism.

mechanisms.name: Group directory in #meta
mechanisms.option: every row with a metadata group
mechanisms.state: Per group in the metadata group: its resource, its incarnation, and its last known replicas and leader. It is a routing hint; the group's own log is the truth.
mechanisms.rules: A group's leader refreshes its record after each change, the newest config winning. A recovery raises the incarnation. A group's record is deleted once the slot table has shown none of its slots for settle.ms and its history is safe.
mechanisms.source: DESIGN-V5 4.2 '#meta' (the shard record), 'A shard is deleted', 'Operator recovery'
mechanisms.precedent: a: TiKV PD's region table (each region's leader reports its peers, leader and region epoch in RegionHeartbeat; PD keeps the report with the newest epoch and hands it to clients as a route; the region's own Raft log stays the truth). For the forced recovery that raises the incarnation: TiKV's unsafe-recover and CockroachDB's 'debug recover'. From memory. | b: TiKV PD's region records, refreshed by each region leader's heartbeat with the newest region epoch winning; CockroachDB's meta2 range descriptors, used as routing hints while the range itself is the truth
mechanisms.why: Both counters agree. a: Same state (per group: last known replicas and leader, as a hint), same rule (the leader refreshes it; the newest config wins), same role (routing). | b: Same state (per group: last known replicas and leader, as a hint), same rules (the leader refreshes it; the newest config wins), same role. cited from memory, sure of the system and the mechanism.

mechanisms.name: Healing by each group's leader
mechanisms.state: Its steps are config entries in the group's own log. It keeps no other state: the target is computed from the ring over the members in #meta, or read from a stored placement.
mechanisms.rules: From its own links the leader adds a learner when a voter is gone, promotes it once caught up, then removes the gone or surplus voter once the voters left answer and hold the commit offset; it grows before it shrinks (A-01, A-19). It hands leadership back to the preferred leader after settle.ms.
mechanisms.model: E-16: 14 rules by ablation (16 of 17 mutants caught); v5-spec/healing.py checked the draft's text before A-01 and A-19
mechanisms.source: SPACE 2 C `self`, SPACE 3 R1.H; DESIGN-V5 4.2 'Healing'; AMENDMENTS A-19, A-01 (5)
mechanisms.precedent: a: CockroachDB's replicate queue (pkg/kv/kvserver/replicate_queue.go with the allocator): each range's leaseholder, with no controller, replaces a voter on a dead store by adding a learner, promoting it once it has caught up, then removing the old voter; filterUnremovableReplicas refuses a removal that would leave too few up-to-date voters; GetNeededVoters keeps the voter count odd. Kafka's preferred-leader election for the hand-back. The target by rendezvous hashing is Thaler and Ravishankar (1998), as Dynamo's ring picks a key's replicas. Function names are from memory; the order 'up-replicate, then remove once the new replica has caught up' is in CockroachDB's replication-layer doc (found by search). | b: CockroachDB's replicate queue and allocator, run by each range's leaseholder (pkg/kv/kvserver/replicate_queue.go; allocatorimpl Allocator.ComputeAction: AddVoter, ReplaceDeadVoter, RemoveDeadVoter, RemoveVoter, RemoveLearner; filterUnremovableReplicas keeps a removal from leaving too few live, caught-up voters); Kafka's preferred leader election for the hand-back after settle.ms
mechanisms.why: Both counters agree. a: Same state (none of its own: each step is a membership entry in the group's log), same step rules (add a learner, promote when caught up, then remove; never remove while the voters left are short), same role (each group's leader repairs its own replicas). What differs is the input: fero reads 'gone' from the leader's own links and ranks members by a hash, where CockroachDB reads a shared liveness record and scores stores. I count those as inputs (the failure detector is link-pings; the target is a policy), not as new state or new safety rules. A close call: SPACE's estimate is 1, and the draft's own text had 9 gaps (healing.py) that CockroachDB's rules would have closed. By DEV-10 (a)'s letter healing has no state of its own: it is a set of rules on raft-config. | b: It keeps no state of its own. E-16's 14 rules (add a learner when a voter is gone; promote a caught-up learner from three to four; remove a voter gone to the leader; remove a surplus voter only once the others answer and hold the commit offset; grow before shrink) are the allocator's actions and guards, in the same role: every group's leader heals, with no controller. The ring only ranks the candidates. SPACE counted 1 because fero wrote the text itself; DEV-10 (b) asks for a precedent, and there is one. cited from memory, sure of the system and the mechanism.

mechanisms.name: Controller loop with commands checked by config epoch
mechanisms.state: The controller's list of live commands in the metadata group, each naming the group's config epoch it was decided at.
mechanisms.rules: The loop on #meta's leader (or a separate controller) decides each change from its own links and the reported config, and writes a command. The group's leader runs it only if the epoch still matches and its own links agree (gone for a removal, alive for a promotion); a command the group refuses times out (A-20).
mechanisms.model: E-16: 18 rules by ablation (16 with a counterexample; 12 of 21 mutants caught, 9 undecided)
mechanisms.source: SPACE 2 C `cent`, `cent-co`, SPACE 3 R1.C; AMENDMENTS A-20, A-19 (reasoned for PD, ISR, SLOG, OBJ); TiKV PD's region epoch and operator timeout
mechanisms.precedent: a: TiKV PD's operators (pd, pkg/schedule/operator: AddLearner, PromoteLearner and RemovePeer steps, one operator per region, sent to the region's leader, refused there when the region epoch has changed, dropped on a timeout), with TiKV's own check at the leader that the voters left healthy still make a quorum (raftstore, check_conf_change). Kafka KRaft's reassignment records are a durable list of the same kind. From memory; E-16 cites the same. | b: TiKV PD operators (one per region, built on a region epoch, dropped on timeout) with TiKV's checks where the command runs (the region epoch check; raftstore check_conf_change refuses a change that would leave no healthy quorum); Kafka KRaft keeps reassignments as records in the metadata log, checked by partition epoch
mechanisms.why: Both counters agree. a: Same state in the same role (the controller's one pending change per group, named by the group's config epoch), same rules (the epoch check where it runs; a timeout). Two differences: fero keeps the list in #meta where PD keeps it in memory, and E-16 added two re-checks of who is alive on the leader's own links. TiKV re-checks health at the leader too, so I count it as published. | b: Same state (pending commands, each tied to the config epoch it was decided at), same rules (run only on a matching epoch; the group's leader checks again with what only it knows; a refused command times out), same role. The form of the leader's re-check differs a little (gone or alive on its own links here; a healthy quorum in TiKV). cited from memory, sure of the system and the mechanism.

mechanisms.name: Planner hints, checked against the config they name
mechanisms.option: self+p (and owed by COMP for DEP-17)
mechanisms.state: Hints written to #meta (drain, retire and gone marks on member records; the planner's lease row in the cluster record), and a placement target and preferred leader stored in the group's log. A move hint takes the move lease like any mover.
mechanisms.rules: Anything holding the admin key sends a hint that names the group config it read. The group applies it only if its config is still that one, else refuses stale-plan; a leader whose link to a member is up ignores a gone hint. A lease row keeps two planners apart.
mechanisms.source: SPACE 2 C `self+p`, SPACE 3 R1.H.P; DESIGN-V5 4.2 'The planner'; AMENDMENTS section 4 (COMP's table lists it as owed; not modelled; K-08); v5-spec/healing.py had the draft's hints
mechanisms.precedent: CockroachDB, a cluster that heals itself with no planner and takes operator commands: node drain (gives up leases, keeps replicas), node decommission and recommission (a mark in the liveness record; each range's replicate queue then moves replicas off), zone configs with constraints and lease_preferences (a stored target and a preferred leaseholder that each range's leaseholder follows), and AdminChangeReplicasRequest.exp_desc ('If the range descriptor is not identical to ExpDesc ... the request will fail', pkg/kv/kvpb/api.proto, read at the source on 2026-11-10). A lease row that keeps two deciders apart is Kubernetes' leader-election Lease.
mechanisms.why: Referee. Every piece of state has a placed match in one system, CockroachDB, in the same role: an optional outside hand on a cluster that heals itself. The stale-plan rule is exp_desc, checked at the source. What b found unmatched: (1) the gone guard, where a leader whose link to that life is up ignores the hint. That is meta-members' own rule (a gone mark is cleared when that life comes back), applied where the hint lands, and both counters judge meta-members not novel. (2) The placement target is kept in the group's own log, not in a system table: same state and role, another home. The planner's lease row is its own row, apart from the move lease (a's regrouping, taken), and a move hint still takes the move lease. It was never modelled (K-08): that is a debt to DEV-03, not novelty. A close call. State names changed by a regrouping the referee took (see disagreements).

mechanisms.name: Log replicas (the witness): lead only to repair
mechanisms.state: Which voters of a group are log replicas: they vote and keep the log tail, but never fold rows or serve clients.
mechanisms.rules: A log replica stands only when no full voter has won an election for twice election.ms. When it leads it commits an entry of its own term, brings a full voter up to date (or adds one from the object store's snapshot and its own tail), hands it leadership, and takes no client write.
mechanisms.source: SPACE 2 V `+wit`, SPACE 3 R1.W; DESIGN-V5 4.2 'Log replicas'; Spanner's witness replicas; never modelled in this study (AMENDMENTS section 2 V, G-25)
mechanisms.precedent: None (both counters). Nearest: witnesses that vote and keep the log but hold no rows (Harp, Spanner, Megastore) never lead; here a log replica leads, only to repair. TiKV's witness could not be checked by either counter.
mechanisms.why: Both counters agree. a: Witnesses that vote and keep a log but hold no rows are published: Harp (Liskov et al., SOSP 1991), Spanner's witness replicas (Spanner docs: they vote and cannot become leader), TiKV's witness. None of them lets the witness lead. fero's rule is that a log replica does lead, but only to repair: it stands when no full voter has won for twice the election time, brings a full voter up to date or builds one from the object store's snapshot and its own tail, hands over, and takes no client write. In Raft the log flows only from the leader, so this rule is what makes a Raft witness work, and I found no paper or system that has it (search: TiKV refuses to hand leadership to a witness, tikv PR 17643; its docs site was not reachable from here). It was never modelled in this study (G-25). Novel. | b: The state has precedents: Spanner's and Megastore's witness replicas vote and keep the log but hold no rows. The rule does not: those witnesses never lead, and here a log replica leads, only to repair (commit an entry of its own term, bring a full voter up, hand over). TiKV's witness may be close, but I could not check it today (docs.pingcap.com is not reachable from this session), so it does not count. Never modelled in this study.

mechanisms.name: Groups owned by the project (pslot)
mechanisms.state: Per project group: its settings class (copies, durability) and the (resource, slot set) pairs it holds.
mechanisms.rules: A new resource's slots start inside an existing group of its class; a different copies or durability forces a group boundary; slot moves split slots off under load, and each move entry names (resource, slot).
mechanisms.model: E-17b, E-17c: the move needs 28 rules, the same as `slot` on the same footing (0 more); about 2 placement rules are reasoned, not modelled
mechanisms.source: SPACE 2 G `pslot`, SPACE 3 R1.P; AMENDMENTS section 2 G and D4; E-36 (measured, with one slot map shared by the project)
mechanisms.precedent: a: CockroachDB's span-config coalescing (cluster setting spanconfig.storage_coalesce_adjacent.enabled: neighbouring tables with the same span config share one range, a different config forces a range boundary, and load-based splitting cuts a busy part off); TiKV PD's schedule.enable-cross-table-merge; YugabyteDB's colocated tables. Setting names are from memory (a search did not show them); SPACE cites the same two. | b: CockroachDB's span-config coalescing (spanconfig.storage_coalesce_adjacent.enabled): adjacent tables with equal span configs share one range, and a different config forces a range boundary; TiKV's enable-cross-table-merge
mechanisms.why: Both counters agree. a: Same state (a group holds parts of many tables that share one placement class), same rules (a new small table starts inside an existing group; a different setting forces a boundary; load splits it off), same role. The move rules are slot-move's own (E-17c: 0 more). | b: Same state (a group holds data of many resources of one settings class), same rules (a new resource starts inside an existing group; other settings force a boundary; load splits it off), same role (many small resources without one group each). cited from memory, sure of the system and the mechanism.

mechanisms.name: Project lanes
mechanisms.state: A fixed number of groups per project (64) and the hash that maps every (resource, partition) onto one of them; copies and durability are project-wide.
mechanisms.rules: The lane count is fixed when the project is founded; every write hashes to its lane; a lane never moves, splits or goes away.
mechanisms.model: E-17b: lanes with a range move need 28 rules (30 in a real log); the LANE row holds no range move, so its count is fixN's 13
mechanisms.source: SPACE 2 G `lane`, SPACE 3 R0.N64; V5-UNITS; Redis Cluster, Pulsar bundles
mechanisms.precedent: a: Temporal's and Cadence's history shards (numHistoryShards is fixed when the cluster is made and never changes; every workflow of every namespace hashes onto one shard; each shard has one owner). Also Kafka's __consumer_offsets topic: a fixed 50 partitions that every group hashes onto. From memory. | b: Fixed hash partitioning: Elasticsearch primary shards (the count is fixed when the index is made; hash of the routing key modulo the count); Kafka's default partitioner; Redis Cluster's fixed 16,384 slots shared by every key
mechanisms.why: Both counters agree. a: Same state (a fixed count and a hash), same rules (fixed at founding; every write hashes to its lane; a lane never moves), same role. | b: Same state (a fixed count and a hash), same rules (fixed at founding; never moves), same role. cited from memory, sure of the system and the mechanism.

mechanisms.name: Slot table
mechanisms.state: In #meta, per slot of a resource: the group that holds it open, or is about to. Each write carries a version (slot epoch, move name, writer incarnation, step) and #meta keeps the highest.
mechanisms.rules: The target writes s to B before it opens; after an abort it writes s to A back before A reopens; a recovery writes the row at the slot's new epoch. So the table is never behind an open.
mechanisms.model: E-15 (TLC and slot_move.py): inside the move's 31 rules ('whenever a group holds s open, the table names it')
mechanisms.source: SPACE 2 P `slot`; DESIGN-V5 4.2 'The slot table'; AMENDMENTS A-16 (4,096 slots, a run-length table)
mechanisms.precedent: a: Redis Cluster's slot map (Redis Cluster specification, 'Hash slots configuration propagation': a slot changes owner only on a claim with a higher configEpoch; a migration ends with CLUSTER SETSLOT and an epoch bump); MongoDB's config.chunks (the config server's row per chunk with a chunk version; a migration commits by writing that row, and a donor that failed over reads it to learn whether the move happened). MongoDB from memory. | b: Redis Cluster's slot map with config epochs (cluster spec: a claim for a slot with a greater configEpoch wins; CLUSTER SETSLOT); Couchbase's vBucket map (1,024 vBuckets to nodes, versioned by the cluster manager)
mechanisms.why: Both counters agree. a: The table itself is published: per slot its owner, with a version, the highest version winning, kept by the metadata service and used as a route. What is fero's own is the order of its writes around a move (before the open; back after an abort; at the new epoch after a recovery). Those are steps of the slot move, they sit inside the move's 28 to 31 rules (E-15, E-17c), and I count them once, in slot-move (see regrouped). | b: Same state (per fixed slot, the owner, with a version where the highest wins), same role (routing; MOVED). The order of its writes inside a move belongs to the slot move. cited from memory, sure of the system and the mechanism.

mechanisms.name: Slot move (the move record: export, import, fence, copy, open)
mechanisms.state: The entries of one move in the source's and the target's logs: exporting, importing, fenced(N), the copy and END(N), open, and cancel, abort or unfenced; and the carried set.
mechanisms.rules: The source fences the slot once, on the target's ready report, and takes no write to it from then. The target opens it once, only after the fence, the delta and the carried set are committed in its own log; one decider gives a move up (A-17). The carried set is the slot's sequence and epoch, dedup outcomes and floors, the lock fence table, the srchi marks and the segment names; a new epoch is recorded in the restore mark before use (A-08).
mechanisms.model: E-15: TLC agrees with slot_move.py on 74 runs, 31 rules with unclean recovery, cancel and abort; E-17c: 28 rules by ablation, crash-only, no give-up (26 on the shared bounds; 33 to 34 with one give-up decider), counting the 13 rules of a plain write path (fixN)
mechanisms.source: SPACE 2 P `slot`, SPACE 3 R1.S.M; DESIGN-V5 4.2 'Moving a slot'; AMENDMENTS A-17, A-16, A-08; E-13 (window measured)
mechanisms.precedent: None (both counters). Nearest: MongoDB's moveChunk (it even carries retryable-write history), Couchbase's vBucket takeover, Redis Cluster's MIGRATING and IMPORTING, Spanner's movedir. None has these entries in two Raft logs, the fence as the decision, the once guards, one give-up decider and this carried set; the rules were found here by model checking (E-15, E-17c).
mechanisms.why: Both counters agree. a: The nearest published forms are MongoDB's moveChunk (clone, catch up, a critical section, a commit at the config server; it even carries retryable-write history), Spanner's movedir (Corbett et al., OSDI 2012, section 2.2: copy in the background, then move the rest in one transaction), Redis Cluster's MIGRATING and IMPORTING, and Vitess's cut-over. None has this state and these rules: entries in two Raft groups' logs (exporting, importing, fenced(N), END(N), open, cancel, abort, unfenced), a fence that counts the uncommitted tail, one give-up decider, a reopen in a higher epoch, and a carried set made of fero's own state (sequence and epoch, dedup outcomes and floors, the fence table, srchi marks, segment names). The rules were found by model checking here (8 bugs in the draft's text; 28 to 31 rules), not taken from a paper. Novel, and the biggest one. | b: Novel. Moves of a hash bucket are published (Couchbase's vBucket takeover; MongoDB's moveChunk with its migration coordinator and its carried retryable-write history; Redis Cluster's MIGRATING and IMPORTING), but none has these entries and guards: the fence in the source's log as the decision, the open in the target's log only after the delta and the carried set commit there, one give-up decider, and a carried set of sequence and epoch, dedup floors, the lock fence table, srchi marks and segment names. fero wrote and corrected the protocol itself (E-15, E-17c).

mechanisms.name: Move policy (who decides the moves)
mechanisms.state: No durable state beyond the promise of one move at a time (a lease row in #meta in DRAFT; the mover's one pending proposal elsewhere); load per slot and group is kept in memory.
mechanisms.rules: One slot at a time, from the busiest group to the least loaded, and only when the move wins by a margin (A-18); a grow makes a new group and a shrink deletes one. Run by the controller, by one loop on #meta's leader that only proposes moves (COMP), or by each group's leader (DRAFT).
mechanisms.source: AMENDMENTS A-18 and section 2 P (E-18 simulated as one loop with exact loads); SPACE 3 R1.S.M.A; DESIGN-V5 4.2 'The shard rule'
mechanisms.precedent: a: MongoDB's balancer (it runs on the config server's primary, moves a chunk from the shard with the most to the shard with the least only when the difference passes a migration threshold, and a shard takes part in one migration at a time); TiKV PD's balance-region and hot-region schedulers, with tolerant-size-ratio as the margin; Slicer's weighted-move (Adya et al., OSDI 2016, section 4.4). For a rule that each leader runs alone: CockroachDB's store rebalancer and load-based splitting. From memory. | b: TiKV PD's balance-region and hot-region schedulers (move from the most loaded store to the least, with tolerant-size-ratio as the margin, under schedule limits); CockroachDB's allocator rebalance threshold and load-based splitting and merging; redis-cli --cluster rebalance --cluster-threshold
mechanisms.why: Both counters agree. a: A load policy: one unit at a time, from the busiest to the least loaded, only past a margin. Same rules in the same role. It keeps load in memory only, so by DEV-10 (a)'s letter it is not a mechanism; the one durable piece is DRAFT's lease row per resource. The form that each leader runs alone was never simulated beyond the halving that fails (A-18); that is evidence owed, not novelty. | b: It holds no durable state and no safety rule (A-18), so by DEV-10 (a)'s letter it is no mechanism: 0 in every slot row. The policy itself (one move at a time, busiest to least loaded, only past a margin) is published. cited from memory, sure of the system and the mechanism.

mechanisms.name: Re-key into a new generation
mechanisms.state: The entries of one re-key (rk, cut, frz, cp, flip) in the old and the new groups' logs, and the catalog's generation pointer.
mechanisms.rules: Copy every partition into a new generation with more groups, freeze the old one, then flip the catalog pointer once the copies are committed; one re-key at a time. A cursor of another generation is refused and restarts from a snapshot.
mechanisms.model: E-17, E-17c: 35 rules by ablation as written, 29 with positions carried (36 to 38 and 30 to 32 in a real log), counting fixN's 13
mechanisms.source: SPACE 2 P `rekey`, SPACE 3 R1.F16.K; V5-PRIMITIVE; Vitess resharding; AMENDMENTS section 2 P (fails SC-08 b and f, model-checked)
mechanisms.precedent: None with the same rules. Nearest: Vitess Reshard (VReplication copies, SwitchTraffic stops writes and flips the routing rules) and MongoDB's reshardCollection (clone, a short write block, a catalog swap). They do the same job by other rules.
mechanisms.why: Referee, judged as the slot move is. a's precedents do the same job: copy into a new layout, stop writes, flip the catalog. Both counters reject the same kind of match for the slot move (MongoDB's moveChunk, Redis Cluster's migration, Couchbase's takeover), because its entries and guards are fero's own. The re-key is the same case. Its entries (rk, cut, frz, cp, flip) live in two groups' Raft logs. It carries dedup and fence state across the flip, and it refuses a cursor of another generation. Its rules were found and counted here (E-17: 35 rules, 22 beyond fixN's 13). If Vitess were a precedent for this, MongoDB's moveChunk would be one for the slot move. CELL only.

mechanisms.name: Split (the split record)
mechanisms.state: The entries of one split in the parent's and the child's logs (spl, and init with the carried dedup and fence state).
mechanisms.rules: A group splits only a range it holds. The parent takes no write to the split-off range once the split entry is in its log; the child starts once, from a committed split, carrying dedup and fence state. A split copies no rows.
mechanisms.model: E-17b, E-17c: split + merge needs 33 rules by ablation (37 in a real log): a 9-rule split, an 11-rule merge and lineage, counting fixN's 13
mechanisms.source: SPACE 2 P `split`, SPACE 3 R1.X; DESIGN-V5 decision 20a; CockroachDB, TiKV
mechanisms.precedent: a: TiKV's region split (the BatchSplit admin command goes through the region's Raft log; each replica that applies it makes the child's peer from its own data, so nothing is copied); CockroachDB's AdminSplit with its split trigger, which also hands the child its share of per-range state (the abort span). From memory. | b: CockroachDB's AdminSplit and split trigger (pkg/kv/kvserver/batcheval/cmd_end_transaction.go: the right-hand range starts once, from the committed split; no rows are copied; per-range state such as the abort span is copied to it); TiKV's BatchSplit
mechanisms.why: Both counters agree. a: Same state (a split entry in the parent's log and the child's first state), same rules, same role. SPLIT is 'CockroachDB-style' by its own source (decision 20a). | b: Same state (a split entry in the parent's log), same rules (split only what you hold; the parent stops taking writes to the split-off range; the child starts once and carries per-range request state), same role. cited from memory, sure of the system and the mechanism.

mechanisms.name: Merge (the merge record)
mechanisms.state: The entries of one merge (mrg, sub, mgd) in the two groups' logs.
mechanisms.rules: The group to be removed freezes only for a committed merge; the survivor takes its rows and carried state once and gives the merged range a new generation.
mechanisms.model: E-17b, E-17c: an 11-rule merge inside split + merge's 33 rules (37 in a real log)
mechanisms.source: SPACE 2 P `split` (and later merges), SPACE 3 R1.X.M; TiKV region merge
mechanisms.precedent: a: TiKV's region merge (PrepareMerge freezes the source at a committed index; CommitMerge at the target takes its data once; the merged region's epoch rises); CockroachDB's range merge (the Subsume request freezes the right-hand range). From memory. | b: TiKV's region merge (PrepareMerge freezes the source, CommitMerge runs in the target, RollbackMerge); CockroachDB's AdminMerge with Subsume
mechanisms.why: Both counters agree. a: Same state, rules and role. PD only. | b: Same state, same rules (the removed group freezes; the survivor takes its rows once), same role. cited from memory, sure of the system and the mechanism.

mechanisms.name: Range table (which group holds which range)
mechanisms.state: Per group: the key or hash range it holds and a generation that rises on every split or merge (CockroachDB's range descriptors; the version half of TiKV's region epoch).
mechanisms.rules: A split or a merge writes the new ranges with a higher generation; a route or a command made on an older generation is refused and refreshed.
mechanisms.source: SPACE 2 P `split` and O `off+lin` (precedent: CockroachDB range descriptors); SPACE 2 C `cent` (PD's region epoch)
mechanisms.precedent: a: CockroachDB's range descriptors, with a generation that rises on every split and merge; TiKV's region epoch (its version half). | b: CockroachDB's range descriptors with a generation that rises on every split and merge; TiKV's region epoch (version)
mechanisms.why: Both counters agree. a: Same state, rule and role. The list names both itself. | b: Same state, same rules (an older generation is refused and refreshed), same role. cited from memory, sure of the system and the mechanism.

mechanisms.name: Split policy (who decides the splits and merges)
mechanisms.state: No durable state: size and load per group, kept in memory.
mechanisms.rules: A group splits when it passes a size or load limit: each leader decides in SPLIT; in PD the controller's schedulers also decide merges. It is listed so that splits are counted as A-18 counts slot moves.
mechanisms.source: DESIGN-V5 decision 20a (SPACE 4.2 SPLIT: 'split by size and load, with no controller'); AMENDMENTS A-18 (a load policy is counted the same wherever it lives)
mechanisms.precedent: a: CockroachDB's size-based and load-based splitting (range_max_bytes; kv.range_split.by_load_enabled), decided by each range's leaseholder, and its merge queue; TiKV's split checker and PD's merge checker. | b: CockroachDB's split queue (by size and by load) run by each leaseholder, and its merge queue; PD's merge checker
mechanisms.why: Both counters agree. a: Same rules in the same role. No durable state: by DEV-10 (a)'s letter a policy, not a mechanism. | b: No durable state. Same rules, same role. cited from memory, sure of the system and the mechanism.

mechanisms.name: Slot sequence
mechanisms.state: Per slot: the last sequence number stamped, read with the slot's epoch. A position is (epoch, sequence); versions, cursors and fence tokens are positions.
mechanisms.rules: The slot's writer stamps each record with the slot's next sequence. The sequence never goes back and travels with the slot.
mechanisms.model: E-15, E-17c: inside the move's rules (1 rule carries the sequence; 'no sequence is stamped by two groups'); E-31: cursors must be per-slot sequences (group offsets break in 5 steps)
mechanisms.source: REQUIREMENTS DEV-10 (a)'s own example; SPACE 2 O `slot`, SPACE 3 R1.S; DESIGN-V5 4.3 'The record'; AMENDMENTS A-16; E-19 (cost measured)
mechanisms.precedent: a: Couchbase's per-vBucket sequence numbers and vBucket UUIDs (kv_engine, docs/dcp/documentation: commands/failover-log.md and commands/stream-request.md; confirmed by search). Each of the 1,024 vBuckets has its own sequence that only rises. A position is (vBucket UUID, seqno). The UUID changes when a vBucket becomes active or stops uncleanly, so no position names two histories. The sequence stays with the vBucket when it moves to another node. DCP cursors and mutation tokens are these positions. | b: Couchbase DCP (kv_engine docs/dcp): every mutation in a vBucket, one of 1,024 fixed hash buckets, gets that vBucket's next sequence number from the active node; a position is (vBucket UUID, seqno) with a failover log; the numbers and the failover log go with the vBucket when it moves between nodes. Kafka's (leader epoch, offset) per partition is the same pair (KIP-101, KIP-320)
mechanisms.why: Both counters agree. a: Same state (per fixed hash bucket: a last sequence, read with an epoch-like id), same rules (the bucket's one writer stamps the next number; it never goes back; it travels with the bucket; a reader ahead of the history is rolled back), same role (versions and cursors that survive a move). This is a specific match, not 'Raft has a log'. SPACE itself names Couchbase's 1,024 vBuckets as the precedent for P `slot`, with nodes in the place of groups. One difference: each vBucket has its own replication stream, where a fero slot shares its group's Raft log; that belongs to G and P, not to this state. That fence tokens are also positions is lock-rows' rule. | b: Same state (the last sequence per fixed slot, read with an epoch of the slot's history), same rules (the slot's one writer stamps the next number; it never goes back; it travels with the slot), same role (positions for cursors and versions that survive a move). DESIGN-V5 10.2 and SPACE call it new ('1 small'); DEV-10 (b) asks for a precedent, and this is a per-slot sequence in production, not just 'a log'. Close call. checked on the web on 2026-11-10 (Couchbase's blog and DCP docs: seqno per vBucket, vBucket UUID, failover log).

mechanisms.name: Lineage
mechanisms.state: Kept for ever: for each group made by a split, its parent and the offset base at which it took over.
mechanisms.rules: A base is written once, when the child starts. A reader's cursor of (generation, group, offset) is resolved through the lineage from the parent to the child.
mechanisms.model: E-17b, E-17c: 2 lineage rules on the shared bounds, 3 with a reader across a merge
mechanisms.source: SPACE 2 O `off+lin` (1: lineage resolution, kept forever); V5-UNITS
mechanisms.precedent: a: Amazon Kinesis shard lineage (Kinesis API: a Shard has ParentShardId, AdjacentParentShardId and a SequenceNumberRange; a consumer finishes the parent before it reads the children); DynamoDB Streams' shard lineage; Pravega's segment successors. | b: Amazon Kinesis shards (API type Shard: ParentShardId, AdjacentParentShardId, SequenceNumberRange.StartingSequenceNumber; a reader finishes the parent, then goes on in the children); DynamoDB Streams has the same; Pravega's segment successors
mechanisms.why: Both counters agree. a: Same state (per child: its parent and where it took over), same rule (a cursor is resolved from the parent to the child), same role. SPLIT only. | b: Same state (per child, its parent and the position it starts at), same rules (written once when the child starts; a reader's cursor is resolved from parent to child), same role. Kinesis keeps it for the retention time, not for ever. cited from memory, sure of the system and the mechanism.

mechanisms.name: Timestamp positions with closed timestamps
mechanisms.state: Per group: a closed timestamp below which no new write will commit; positions are commit timestamps.
mechanisms.rules: The leader advances the closed timestamp as the locks below it resolve; replicas serve reads and change feeds at or below it.
mechanisms.source: SPACE 2 O `hlc` (1: closed timestamps); CockroachDB's closed timestamps, TiKV's resolved timestamp
mechanisms.precedent: a: CockroachDB's closed timestamps (RFC 20180603_follower_reads.md); TiKV's resolved-ts. | b: CockroachDB's closed timestamps; TiKV's resolved timestamp
mechanisms.why: Both counters agree. a: Same state, rules and role. PD only. | b: The published mechanism, as PD's row takes it. cited from memory, sure of the system and the mechanism.

mechanisms.name: Judging at the one writer (conditions, ops, claim, batch)
mechanisms.state: Not durable: the writer's log-end state, the fold of its committed state plus its uncommitted tail. Only results are appended.
mechanisms.rules: Dedup, shape checks, rules, conditions and ops are judged against the log-end state, in that order, and only for a slot this group holds open. Every answer, a refusal and an empty claim included, is sent only once the log end it was judged on has committed (A-04); a deposed writer answers unknown.
mechanisms.source: SPACE 2 K; DESIGN-V5 4.3 'At the writer' and 'Two states on the writer'; AMENDMENTS A-04 (2 rules; every row but BUY); E-22, E-22b (measured in a simulation with Porcupine, Knossos and Elle)
mechanisms.precedent: a: ZooKeeper's request pipeline (Hunt et al., USENIX ATC 2010, section 4.1, and PrepRequestProcessor.java: the leader judges each request against its future state, that is its state plus the proposals not yet committed, turns it into an idempotent transaction, and the followers apply the result; a request that fails becomes an error transaction that is ordered and answered after commit). Also CockroachDB's proposer-evaluated KV (RFC 20160420_proposer_evaluated_kv.md). | b: ZooKeeper's request pipeline (PrepRequestProcessor judges each request against its outstanding, not yet committed changes and proposes only the resulting state change; every answer, an error included, leaves in commit order; Junqueira, Reed and Serafini, 'Zab', DSN 2011); CockroachDB's proposer-evaluated KV (RFC 20160420); Kafka's group coordinator runtime (KIP-848), which holds an answer until its records commit
mechanisms.why: Both counters agree. a: Same state (the leader's state plus its uncommitted tail, not durable), same rules (judge at the one writer; append only results; answer after commit), same role. A-04's rule that a refusal waits for the log end it was judged on is ZooKeeper's error transaction. By DEV-10 (a)'s letter it has no durable state. | b: No durable state. Same rules (judge on the log-end state; append results only; answer only after the judged log end commits), same role. cited from memory, sure of the system and the mechanism.

mechanisms.name: Dedup window (issuer window, floor, outcomes by id, per-hop time budgets)
mechanisms.state: Per group, tagged by slot: per issuer the highest call id seen and every committed outcome above the floor; an issuer silent for the retry horizon is forgotten.
mechanisms.rules: An attempt among the outcomes gets its first answer; one at or below the floor (highest id minus the window) is refused stale-attempt; a resent attempt's refusal is appended. Each copy carries a time budget that every hop cuts, and a relay forwards a copy once.
mechanisms.model: E-20: 17 rules by ablation (19 under `fwd`)
mechanisms.source: SPACE 2 D `win`; DESIGN-V5 4.3 'Dedup'; AMENDMENTS section 2 D; E-44 (measured: a window alone fails past its horizon)
mechanisms.precedent: None (both counters). Its parts are known (Kafka's last five batches per producer, NFSv4.1's session slots, deadlines cut at each hop); the set (a floor at the highest id minus a window, refusals of resends kept as outcomes, per-hop time budgets, forward-once) is the draft's own.
mechanisms.why: Both counters agree. a: Its parts have cousins: Kafka keeps a producer's last five batches (KIP-98), NFSv4.1 keeps one reply per session slot (RFC 5661, section 2.10.6), and Liskov, Shrira and Wroclawski (1991) forget old connections by bounding how late a message can arrive. No paper or system has this set: a floor at the highest id minus a window, over ids that may have gaps; the refusals of resent attempts appended as outcomes; a time budget that every hop cuts; forward-once. SPACE names no precedent but the draft, and it took three review rounds. Novel. | b: Novel. The parts are known (Kafka keeps the last five batches per producer; deadlines are cut hop by hop in gRPC), but the composition (issuer window, floor, outcomes by id, and per-hop time budgets as the reason a forgotten issuer is safe) is the draft's own, 17 to 19 rules after three review rounds (E-20). No system has the same state and rules.

mechanisms.name: Client sessions
mechanisms.state: A session registry (#sessions: per client life, a lease it renews), and per group, tagged by slot: per session the outcomes at or above the client's floor (its lowest unacknowledged id), and that floor.
mechanisms.rules: Apply an attempt only when it is not among the session's outcomes, above its floor, and while the session lives; a copy at or below the floor is answered stale. A session expires by the registry's writer time, and unknown is answered only once that expiry has committed; a restarted process takes a new session. Under `fwd` a relay forwards a copy once (A-21).
mechanisms.model: E-20: 13 rules by ablation (14 under `fwd`, the hop rule partly reasoned)
mechanisms.source: SPACE 2 D `sess`; Raft thesis 6.3, LogCabin; AMENDMENTS A-21, A-04 (a session-bound write waits for its session's record)
mechanisms.precedent: a: Ongaro's thesis, section 6.3 (a session per client, serial numbers, cached answers; the client's lowest unanswered number lets the server drop older answers; sessions expire by a time agreed through the log), and LogCabin. RIFL (Lee et al., SOSP 2015, sections 3 and 4: completion records per client, the client's first incomplete id, client leases at one lease server, and completion records that move with the object when it migrates). | b: Ongaro's thesis section 6.3 (a session per client, a serial number per request, cached answers, the client's lowest unanswered number as the floor, expiry by a time agreed through the log); LogCabin
mechanisms.why: Both counters agree. a: Same state (a lease registry, and per group the outcomes above each client's floor), same rules, same role. RIFL has the two things the thesis lacks: a registry apart from the data, and records carried on a move. forward.once is how etcd's raft forwards a proposal: once, and the client retries. | b: Same state, same rules, same role. The registry apart from the per-group tables is how Kafka splits producer ids (handed out centrally) from per-partition state. cited from memory, sure of the system and the mechanism.

mechanisms.name: Producer id, epoch and sequence
mechanisms.state: Per (producer, partition): the producer's epoch and last sequence, with its last cached batches; producer ids are handed out by the controller.
mechanisms.rules: Accept the next sequence, absorb a duplicate, refuse a gap. A give-up bumps the epoch and restarts the sequence (KIP-360); 'unknown producer' is answered only once the forget has committed (A-22).
mechanisms.model: E-20: 16 rules by ablation (17 under `fwd`)
mechanisms.source: SPACE 2 D `pid`; Kafka KIP-98, KIP-360; AMENDMENTS A-22
mechanisms.precedent: a: Kafka KIP-98 (producer id, epoch and sequence per partition) and KIP-360 (a give-up bumps the epoch). | b: Kafka KIP-98 (producer id, epoch, a sequence per partition, five cached batches) and KIP-360 (a give-up bumps the epoch)
mechanisms.why: Both counters agree. a: It is Kafka's own mechanism. A-22's two fixes are KIP-360's. ISR only. | b: The published mechanism. A-22's second fix (answer 'unknown producer' only once the forget has committed) is A-04's answer rule, published as writer-judging is. cited from memory, sure of the system and the mechanism.

mechanisms.name: Caller keys (idempotency keys for calls)
mechanisms.option: every option (A-10: caller keys beside it)
mechanisms.state: Per caller key, for its ttl: a claim with a lease, and the first result (a row in #calls, or a session per call).
mechanisms.rules: A call with a key claims its row before its handler runs and stores the result; a retry gets the first result. A re-run after the lease lapses issues the same attempt ids, under a fence on the key.
mechanisms.model: E-20 modelled the `keys` option alone (12 rules by ablation); a caller key beside `sess` or `win` was not modelled
mechanisms.source: AMENDMENTS A-10 (five API changes; TEST-03) and section 4 (COMP's table); DESIGN-V5 4.5 'Call keys'; Stripe, SQS dedup ids; for V4 it would apply only if v4 were built on
