mechanisms.why: Both counters agree. a: Same state, rules and role. OBJ only. | b: Same state (a lease end and an epoch in one compare-and-swap register), same rules, same role. cited from memory, sure of the system and the mechanism.

mechanisms.name: Lanes (per-origin logs)
mechanisms.state: Per author (a member's life): its own numbered log of the changes it stamped, kept by every replica that holds the rows.
mechanisms.rules: An author stamps each change with its next ticket in its own lane; replicas copy lanes in ticket order; a restarted member writes under a new lane.
mechanisms.source: REQUIREMENTS section 5 (v4's 13 novel kernel mechanisms; DESIGN-V5 10.1, 10.2); CLAUDE.md (per-origin logs); kernel/log.ts
mechanisms.precedent: a: Bayou (Petersen et al., SOSP 1997, sections 3 and 4: each server's writes carry its id and accept stamp; servers pass them on in that order, so whoever holds one write of a server holds every earlier one); Golding's timestamped anti-entropy (Golding, 1992: a message log per originating site). | b: Bayou (Petersen et al., 'Flexible Update Propagation for Weakly Consistent Replication', SOSP 1997: each server's writes carry its own rising accept stamp and every server holds a prefix of each other server's writes); Golding's timestamped anti-entropy (UCSC thesis, 1992): one message log per originator
mechanisms.why: Both counters agree. a: Same state (a numbered log per author, kept by every holder), same rules (the author numbers its changes; others copy them in order), same role. A new lane for a restarted member is a detail. | b: Same state (a numbered log per author, held by the replicas), same rules (the author stamps; replicas copy in order), same role (leaderless replication). Judged from the list's text of v4; the code was not re-read. REQUIREMENTS section 5 counts it among v4's 13 without a precedent test. cited from memory, sure of the system and the mechanism.

mechanisms.name: Stamps (per-cell last writer wins)
mechanisms.state: Per cell: the stamp of the change that holds it now: member-list version, ticket number, author.
mechanisms.rules: A change replaces a cell's value only if its stamp is newer: version first, then ticket, then author.
mechanisms.source: REQUIREMENTS section 5 (v4's 13 novel kernel mechanisms; DESIGN-V5 10.1, 10.2); SPACE 2 O `lamp`; CLAUDE.md (per-cell LWW and Lamport clocks)
mechanisms.precedent: a: Thomas's write rule (Thomas, ACM TODS 1979) with Lamport's total order (Lamport, CACM 1978: a counter, then the site id); the last-writer-wins register (Shapiro et al., 2011). | b: The last-writer-wins register (Shapiro et al., 'A comprehensive study of Convergent and Commutative Replicated Data Types', 2011) with Lamport's total order (1978); Cassandra's per-cell timestamps; the (view, counter) order of viewstamps (Oki and Liskov, PODC 1988)
mechanisms.why: Both counters agree. a: Same state (a stamp per cell), same rule (a change wins only if its stamp is newer), same role. Putting the member-list version in front still gives one total order and one rule. | b: Same state (a stamp per cell), same rule (the newer stamp wins), same role. Judged from the list's text of v4; the code was not re-read. REQUIREMENTS section 5 counts it among v4's 13 without a precedent test. cited from memory, sure of the system and the mechanism.

mechanisms.name: Digests (anti-entropy)
mechanisms.state: Per link: a short list, for each author, of the highest ticket this replica holds.
mechanisms.rules: After hello, and again after a paused link drains, the two sides swap digests and send what the other lacks.
mechanisms.source: REQUIREMENTS section 5 (v4's 13 novel kernel mechanisms; DESIGN-V5 10.1, 10.2); CLAUDE.md (digest anti-entropy)
mechanisms.precedent: a: Bayou's anti-entropy by version vectors (SOSP 1997, section 3); Golding's summary vectors (1992). | b: Bayou's version vectors in anti-entropy (SOSP 1997); Scuttlebutt digests (van Renesse et al., LADIS 2008), as Cassandra's gossip sends them
mechanisms.why: Both counters agree. a: Same state (per author, the highest number held), same rule (swap, then send what the other lacks), same role. | b: Same state (per author, the highest number held), same rules (swap, then send what the other lacks), same role. Judged from the list's text of v4; the code was not re-read. REQUIREMENTS section 5 counts it among v4's 13 without a precedent test. cited from memory, sure of the system and the mechanism.

mechanisms.name: Tombstones
mechanisms.state: Per removed cell: a deleted-at marker with its stamp.
mechanisms.rules: A removal leaves a marker so that an older late change cannot bring the value back; a marker is dropped only once every holder has shown it is past it.
mechanisms.source: REQUIREMENTS section 5 (v4's 13 novel kernel mechanisms; DESIGN-V5 10.1, 10.2); kernel/log.ts; STATUS V4-31
mechanisms.precedent: a: Wuu and Bernstein, 'Efficient solutions to the replicated log and dictionary problems' (PODC 1984): a delete record is kept until the time table shows that every site has it. | b: Wuu and Bernstein, 'Efficient solutions to the replicated log and dictionary problems', PODC 1984 (a delete record is kept until every node is known to have it); Cassandra's tombstones
mechanisms.why: Both counters agree. a: Same state (a delete marker), same rules (it blocks an older late change; it is dropped only once every holder is known to be past it), same role. | b: Same state (a marker per removed cell), same rules (it blocks an older change; it is dropped once every holder is past it), same role. Judged from the list's text of v4; the code was not re-read. REQUIREMENTS section 5 counts it among v4's 13 without a precedent test. cited from memory, sure of the system and the mechanism.

mechanisms.name: Compaction frontiers
mechanisms.state: Per (author, row): the point below which a replica has compacted its log.
mechanisms.rules: A replica compacts a lane only behind the frontier that every current holder has attested on crash-stable floors.
mechanisms.source: REQUIREMENTS section 5 (v4's 13 novel kernel mechanisms; DESIGN-V5 10.1, 10.2); CLAUDE.md (log compaction behind the holders' crash-stable frontier, V4-57)
mechanisms.precedent: Wuu and Bernstein, 'Efficient solutions to the replicated log and dictionary problems' (PODC 1984): a log record is discarded once the time table shows every site holds it. Golding's acknowledgment vectors (1992).
mechanisms.why: Referee. The frontier is the lowest point every current holder has attested. Dropping the log only behind what every holder has acknowledged is published: same state, same rule, same role. What is v4's own is that the acknowledgment is of crash-stable floors per (author, row), and that is the floors' rule: v4-floors is novel by both counters. DESIGN-V5 10.1's list of protocols with no literature does not name the frontiers; REQUIREMENTS section 5 put them among its 13 without a precedent test.

mechanisms.name: Orphans
mechanisms.state: Per slice: an orphan mark on a copy this replica may no longer serve.
mechanisms.rules: A slice is frozen when its keepers were reassigned away or a cancelled copy left partial data; it is copied again from a teacher, or held only until the new keepers prove they have everything.
mechanisms.source: REQUIREMENTS section 5 (v4's 13 novel kernel mechanisms; DESIGN-V5 10.1, 10.2); tools/debug/eli5.mjs (orphaned)
mechanisms.precedent: None that either counter could name; Riak's ownership handoff is the nearest.
mechanisms.why: Both counters agree. a: Riak's ownership handoff is the nearest published form (the old owner keeps a partition until the new owner has it). I know no paper or system with v4's rule: a slice is frozen, neither served nor dropped, when its keepers were reassigned or a cancelled copy left partial data, and is then re-copied from a teacher or held until the new keepers prove they hold everything. Not sure of a precedent, so novel. | b: No precedent I can name: a frozen slice copy that waits for a teacher or for the new keepers' proof is v4's own. Judged from the list's text of v4; the code was not re-read. REQUIREMENTS section 5 counts it among v4's 13 without a precedent test.

mechanisms.name: Sheds
mechanisms.state: Per slice: that a former keeper deleted its copy; per paused link: that its whole queue was thrown away.
mechanisms.rules: A former keeper sheds a slice only once every current keeper has proved it holds everything; a shed link queue is healed by a new digest exchange.
mechanisms.source: REQUIREMENTS section 5 (v4's 13 novel kernel mechanisms; DESIGN-V5 10.1, 10.2); tools/debug/eli5.mjs (shed)
mechanisms.precedent: None (both counters): a keeper deletes its copy only on its successors' proof by floors, and a paused link's queue is thrown away and healed by a digest. Riak's handoff is the nearest for the first half.
mechanisms.why: Both counters agree. a: Deleting a copy only after the new owners have it is Riak's handoff. But v4's proof is the floors (the pp floor law, which DESIGN-V5 10.1 lists as having no literature), and the same word covers a second state, a link queue thrown away whole. Not sure of a precedent with these rules, so novel. | b: No precedent I can name for a keeper that deletes its copy only on its successors' proof, or for a link queue thrown away and healed by a digest. Judged from the list's text of v4; the code was not re-read. REQUIREMENTS section 5 counts it among v4's 13 without a precedent test.

mechanisms.name: Latches
mechanisms.state: Per slice being copied: the one chosen teacher, with incoming changes for the slice held to one side; per store: a latch set by a failed fsync.
mechanisms.rules: A replica latches onto exactly one teacher and drops copy data from any other; a failed fsync latches the store shut.
mechanisms.source: REQUIREMENTS section 5 (v4's 13 novel kernel mechanisms; DESIGN-V5 10.1, 10.2); DESIGN-V5 10.1 (the teacher latch); tools/debug/eli5.mjs (acquireStart, stageDrop)
mechanisms.precedent: None for the teacher latch (DESIGN-V5 10.1: no literature). Its second half, the fsync latch, is published (PostgreSQL stops on a failed fsync since 2018).
mechanisms.why: Both counters agree. a: DESIGN-V5 10.1 lists the teacher latch among v4's 'protocols with no literature'. The entry also holds a second, unrelated latch: one failed fsync shuts the store. That one is published (PostgreSQL panics on a failed fsync since the 2018 'fsyncgate' fix). See regrouped. | b: DESIGN-V5 10.1 lists the teacher latch among 'protocols with no literature'. Judged from the list's text of v4; the code was not re-read. REQUIREMENTS section 5 counts it among v4's 13 without a precedent test.

mechanisms.name: Teachers
mechanisms.state: Per slice copy: the staged data from the teacher and its end marker.
mechanisms.rules: The teacher ships the part of a slice the learner lacks, then a marker for 'everything up to here'; the learner folds the staged copy in at once, never half.
mechanisms.source: REQUIREMENTS section 5 (v4's 13 novel kernel mechanisms; DESIGN-V5 10.1, 10.2); tools/debug/eli5.mjs (teachShip, acquire)
mechanisms.precedent: None (both counters). Near Raft's InstallSnapshot, but it ships only the part of a slice the learner lacks, and its cut sets the learner's floors (DESIGN-V5 10.1).
mechanisms.why: Both counters agree. a: A staged copy with an end marker, folded in at once, looks like Raft's InstallSnapshot. But here the teacher ships only the part of a slice the learner lacks, its cut sets the learner's floors, and it works only with the teacher latch; DESIGN-V5 10.1 lists that protocol as having no literature. Not sure of a precedent with the same rules, so novel. | b: A staged state transfer with an end marker is close to Raft's InstallSnapshot, but the 'part of a slice the learner lacks' and its tie to latches and floors are v4's own. Not sure, so novel. Judged from the list's text of v4; the code was not re-read. REQUIREMENTS section 5 counts it among v4's 13 without a precedent test.

mechanisms.name: Floors
mechanisms.state: Per (author, row) and holder: a possession floor and a durable floor, below which that holder holds every change.
mechanisms.rules: A holder raises its floors as it receives and syncs changes and attests them to its co-holders (the pp floor law); a teacher's cut sets the learner's floors.
mechanisms.source: REQUIREMENTS section 5 (v4's 13 novel kernel mechanisms; DESIGN-V5 10.1, 10.2); kernel/log.ts; DESIGN-V5 10.1 (the pp floor law)
mechanisms.precedent: None (both counters). Acknowledgment vectors are published (Wuu and Bernstein 1984; Golding 1992); the pp floor law, with a possession and a durable floor per (author, row) and holder, is not (DESIGN-V5 10.1).
mechanisms.why: Both counters agree. a: DESIGN-V5 10.1 lists the pp floor law among v4's 'protocols with no literature'. Acknowledgment vectors are published (Golding 1992), but two floors per (author, row) and holder, with the law that ties them, are v4's own. | b: DESIGN-V5 10.1 lists the pp floor law among 'protocols with no literature'. Acknowledgement matrices are published (Wuu and Bernstein), but not this law per (author, row) with a possession floor and a durable floor. Judged from the list's text of v4; the code was not re-read. REQUIREMENTS section 5 counts it among v4's 13 without a precedent test.

mechanisms.name: FEED words
mechanisms.state: Per feeder and spoke (a client and its primary server): the words the feeder owes the spoke about sheds and re-latches of the rows it feeds.
mechanisms.rules: A feeder tells its spokes when it shed or re-latched rows, so a spoke resyncs and never keeps rows its feeder dropped; an owed word survives a paused link.
mechanisms.source: REQUIREMENTS section 5 (v4's 13 novel kernel mechanisms; DESIGN-V5 10.1, 10.2); kernel/codec.ts (FEED, V4-62); STATUS V4-67
mechanisms.precedent: None (both counters; DESIGN-V5 10.1 lists FEED words among the protocols with no literature).
mechanisms.why: Both counters agree. a: DESIGN-V5 10.1 lists FEED words among v4's 'protocols with no literature'. I know no precedent. | b: DESIGN-V5 10.1 lists FEED words among 'protocols with no literature'. Judged from the list's text of v4; the code was not re-read. REQUIREMENTS section 5 counts it among v4's 13 without a precedent test.

mechanisms.name: In-sync sets
mechanisms.state: Per slice: the holders that have proved they hold everything up to the crash-stable frontier (named in REQUIREMENTS section 5; this reading of v4 was not checked against a model).
mechanisms.rules: A holder enters the set only by attesting its floors, and leaves it when it is reassigned or falls behind.
mechanisms.source: REQUIREMENTS section 5 (v4's 13 novel kernel mechanisms; DESIGN-V5 10.1, 10.2); the state line is this list's reading of v4's holders
mechanisms.precedent: Kafka's in-sync replicas under KRaft (KIP-841, KIP-903): the ISR row carries them as isr-set. v4 itself has no such state.
mechanisms.why: Referee, with v4's code searched. v4 has no such state: kernel/*.ts holds neither 'in-sync', 'insync' nor 'eligible' (searched 2026-11-10). Its holders attest floors (kernel/scope.ts), which v4-floors already counts. The names come from the third v5 draft, Kafka's in-sync sets under a controller (DESIGN-V5 section 12, decision 2c; section 13, 'The third draft'); DESIGN-V5 10.2's 'Gone' list joined them to v4's. So V4 does not carry this unit, and REQUIREMENTS section 5's thirteen hold eleven of v4's own. b judged the list's text, which the list itself says was not checked against v4.

mechanisms.name: Eligible leaders
mechanisms.state: Per row: the members that may take over stamping it after a view change (named in REQUIREMENTS section 5; this reading of v4 was not checked against a model).
mechanisms.rules: Only a member that holds everything the old owner stamped may become the row's owner.
mechanisms.source: REQUIREMENTS section 5 (v4's 13 novel kernel mechanisms; DESIGN-V5 10.1, 10.2); the state line is this list's reading of v4's owner change
mechanisms.precedent: Kafka's eligible leader replicas (KIP-966): the ISR row carries them as eligible-leaders. v4 itself has no such state.
mechanisms.why: Referee, with v4's code searched. v4 has no such state: kernel/*.ts holds neither 'in-sync', 'insync' nor 'eligible' (searched 2026-11-10). Its holders attest floors (kernel/scope.ts), which v4-floors already counts. The names come from the third v5 draft, Kafka's in-sync sets under a controller (DESIGN-V5 section 12, decision 2c; section 13, 'The third draft'); DESIGN-V5 10.2's 'Gone' list joined them to v4's. So V4 does not carry this unit, and REQUIREMENTS section 5's thirteen hold eleven of v4's own. b judged the list's text, which the list itself says was not checked against v4.

mechanisms.name: Membership views by ballot (joint consensus)
mechanisms.state: The member list and its version (the epoch in every stamp); ballots and votes for the next view; held members.
mechanisms.rules: A view changes only by a ballot carried by a majority of the old and of the new view. A member that voted for a view two or more members apart from its own is held, read-only and uncounted, until that ballot settles.
mechanisms.source: SPACE 2 C `self` and SPACE 3 V4 (ballot views); CLAUDE.md (joint-consensus views, V4-6, V4-55, V4-60); not one of the thirteen
mechanisms.precedent: None (both counters). Joint consensus is published (Ongaro's thesis, section 4.3), but not ballots among leaderless members with held members, the knock window and a leave that drops the dead (DESIGN-V5 10.1).
mechanisms.why: Both counters agree. a: Membership by ballots carried by a majority of the old and of the new view is joint consensus (Ongaro's thesis, section 4.3). But v4 adds the hold on a member that voted for a far view (V4-55) and the knock window (V4-39), and DESIGN-V5 10.1 lists both under 'protocols with no literature'. Novel. | b: Joint consensus is published (Raft thesis chapter 4), but v4 runs it as ballots among leaderless members, with held members (DESIGN-V5 10.1: 'no literature') and a leave ballot that drops the dead. Not one of the thirteen.

mechanisms.name: Ring ownership (one owner per row)
mechanisms.state: For each row: the one member that the ring over the current view picks to stamp its changes.
mechanisms.rules: Every write to a row is forwarded to its owner, which stamps and files it; a view change moves ownership.
mechanisms.source: SPACE 2 P `ring`; CLAUDE.md (ring-owned single-writer pipeline); not one of the thirteen
mechanisms.precedent: a: Chord (Stoica et al., SIGCOMM 2001: a key is owned by its successor on the ring, and ownership moves when members change); Dynamo's ring (DeCandia et al., SOSP 2007, section 4.2). | b: Dynamo (DeCandia et al., SOSP 2007, sections 4.2, 4.3 and 4.5: a ring over the members picks the coordinator of a key, and a request is forwarded to it); Riak's vnode-coordinated puts
mechanisms.why: Both counters agree. a: Same state (per key, the one member the ring picks), same rules (send the write to the owner; a membership change moves ownership), same role. | b: Same state (the ring's pick per row), same rules (forward to the owner, which stamps; a view change moves ownership), same role. cited from memory, sure of the system and the mechanism. The referee dropped its read of v4.eligible: v4 has no such state (see v4-eligible-leaders).

mechanisms.name: Confirm ladder (per-write confirmations)
mechanisms.state: Per pending write: which holders have attested that they hold it, in memory or on disk.
mechanisms.rules: A write is answered at the rung it asked for, once enough holders attest it.
mechanisms.source: SPACE 2 Q `mix` (v4's per-write ladder); kernel/confirm.ts; not one of the thirteen
mechanisms.precedent: a: MongoDB's write concern, chosen per write (w: a number or 'majority'; j: true for on disk). | b: MongoDB's write concern per write ({w: n or majority, j: true}: how many members hold it, in memory or on disk); Cassandra's consistency level per write
mechanisms.why: Both counters agree. a: Same state (per pending write, who has it), same rule (answer once enough hold it at the level asked), same role. | b: Same state, same rule (answer once enough holders attest, at the rung asked for), same role. cited from memory, sure of the system and the mechanism.

mechanisms.name: The outside log (NATS JetStream), bought
mechanisms.state: Everything the bought system keeps: replicated streams with their sequences, its own consensus groups and metadata, its message-id dedup window, consumers and their acks, key-value buckets.
mechanisms.rules: Theirs. fero publishes with an expected sequence for a condition, reads streams to fold rows, and uses consumers for delivery; failover, dedup, placement, storage and time are the bought system's.
mechanisms.source: SPACE 4.1 BUY and footnote 12, SPACE 3 BUY; E-44 (measured: four patterns in 164 fero-owned lines; ten gaps)
mechanisms.precedent: a: NATS JetStream itself, a production system. | b: NATS JetStream itself (a bought production system; E-44 ran fero's patterns on 2.10.22)
mechanisms.why: Both counters agree. a: Bought, not designed: 0 in L1, as SPACE says. BUY only. | b: Everything in it is the bought system's own published work, so nothing here is fero's to count.

mechanisms.name: One process per dir: a lock with a lease, and an epoch fence
mechanisms.option: the draft's L0, on no SPACE axis: every row whose members keep their own dirs takes it (SPACE 4, "The rule")
mechanisms.state: Per dir: a lock file with the holder's record (pid, host, start) and a lease that the holder renews from a thread of its own; the lease's epoch, carried in the name of every file; retired-<epoch> directories, each with a boot record that names the end offset the new holder will read to.
mechanisms.rules: A process takes a dir only when the lock is free or its holder is gone (its pid gone, or its lease run out), and it takes a new epoch. A holder writes only files of its own epoch. A new holder renames the old epoch's directory to retired-<epoch>, writes and fsyncs a boot record that names it and the end offset, and only then reads it, read-only and never past that end. Files roll by a new file and an unlink, never by truncating in place.
mechanisms.model: Not modelled in this study.
mechanisms.source: DESIGN-V5 4.1 "One process per dir"; STATUS V4-59 (v4's lock file with a lease: four review rounds); CLAUDE.md (shell: one process at a time holds a durable dir)
mechanisms.precedent: None that a counter placed. The lock with a lease alone is published (npm's proper-lockfile; sanlock's delta leases); the epoch fence is not.
mechanisms.why: Added by a; taken. The list missed it: durable state (a lock file with a lease, epoch-named files, retired directories, a boot record with the end offset) with rules of its own, in DESIGN-V5 4.1 (L0). b did not list it. The lock with a lease alone is published, so V4, which has only that (V4-59), does not carry this unit. The fence, which stops a holder frozen past its lease from changing what the new holder reads, has no precedent that either counter placed, so by DEV-10 (b) it is novel. Every row that keeps fero's own dirs carries it: +1 in each of 16 rows, so it changes no order among them. PD (RocksDB's own lock), OBJ (no durable dir of its own), V4 and BUY do not. The referee knows one lead that no counter placed, so it does not count here: HBase renames a dead region server's WAL directory to '-splitting' and recovers each file's HDFS lease before it reads the logs (from memory, not checked).

mechanisms.name: Repair of a damaged entry from a peer (Z par)
mechanisms.option: par (no row takes it; AMENDMENTS section 4 scores COMP+par beside COMP)
mechanisms.state: Per entry: a checksum and a bad mark; per group: which damaged entries may be the only committed copy.
mechanisms.rules: A replica that finds a damaged entry marks it bad, keeps its vote, and fetches the entry from a peer. While the entry may be the only committed copy, the replica does not stand and does not count toward a commit of it (the "possibly committed" rule).
mechanisms.model: E-37 (TLC on etcd's spec, three voters, no membership change): 7 rules, each needed; 0 stuck states of 276 two-damage states
mechanisms.source: SPACE 2 Z `par`; AMENDMENTS section 2 Z and section 4 ("One add-on the row rule might admit"); E-37
mechanisms.precedent: Alagappan, Ganesan, Lee, Albarghouthi, Chidambaram, Arpaci-Dusseau and Arpaci-Dusseau, "Protocol-Aware Recovery for Consensus-Based Storage" (FAST 2018), sections 3 and 4: CTRL tells a crash from a corruption by checksums, repairs a faulty entry from a peer, and keeps a node with a faulty entry that may be committed from leading. Built into LogCabin (Raft) and ZooKeeper in the paper; TigerBeetle's VSR repairs the same way in production.
mechanisms.why: Added by a; taken with no rows. No row holds Z `par`, so it changes no count. It is here so the judges can score COMP+par (AMENDMENTS section 4). a's precedent is the paper SPACE itself names for the option: same state (a checksum and a bad mark per entry), same rules (repair from a peer; a replica whose damaged entry may be the only committed copy neither stands nor counts toward it), same role. E-37 modelled it: 7 rules, each needed. So COMP+par has COMP's count of novel mechanisms.

mechanisms.name: Consumer groups (#groups: members with leases, a generation, fenced cursors)
mechanisms.option: every row (P-08), as an L5 library
mechanisms.state: In #groups, per group: a row with a lease for each member, and a generation. Per consumer: its committed cursor, a row written under a fence on the generation.
mechanisms.rules: The assignment of groups or slots to members is a pure function of the live members and the generation. A member whose lease lapses by writer time is dropped and the generation rises. A cursor is written only with a fence on the current generation, so a consumer of an older generation cannot commit.
mechanisms.model: E-30 modelled the cursor and the marks, not the membership
mechanisms.source: DESIGN-V5 5.3 "Consumer groups" and 5.1; REQUIREMENTS P-08; E-30 (the cursor rule, with srchi-slot)
mechanisms.precedent: a: Kafka's group coordinator (KIP-62 and KIP-848: members kept by heartbeats under a session timeout, a generation that rises on every change, and an offset commit from an older generation refused with ILLEGAL_GENERATION). | b: Kafka's group coordinator (members kept alive by heartbeats under a session timeout, a generation id, an assignment per generation, OffsetCommit refused with ILLEGAL_GENERATION; KIP-848)
mechanisms.why: Added by both counters, blind, with the same rows and the same precedent: Kafka's group coordinator. Not novel. The state name is cgroup.members (the list's 'group' means a log group). a: The list has srchi-marks, which writes the cursor, but not the group's own rows. Same state (members with leases; a generation; cursors), same rules, same role as Kafka's. Not novel, so it changes no DEV-01 count; it adds to DEV-02's pairs. V4 is left out (no conditions under lww) and BUY (JetStream's own consumers). | b: The list has the cursor (sub.cursor) but not the group's member rows and generation, which are named, replicated state with their own rules. Same state, same rules, same role as Kafka's. cited from memory, sure of the system and the mechanism.

mechanisms.name: Presence: rows that live while a session lives
mechanisms.option: every row that serves presence (rows: { while: 'session' })
mechanisms.state: Per row written `while: 'session'`: the id of the session it lives by. The session is a row in #sessions with a lease the client renews.
mechanisms.rules: Each group's writer follows #sessions. Once a session's lapse has committed there (by #sessions' writer time), the writer removes that session's rows by entries in its own log.
mechanisms.model: Not modelled in this study.
mechanisms.source: DESIGN-V5 5.3 'Presence' and 5.1; AMENDMENTS K-11 (session expiry by #sessions' writer time). The registry exists in the rows with D win, pid and txn too, where the list's client-sessions does not put it.
mechanisms.precedent: a: ZooKeeper's ephemeral nodes (Hunt et al., USENIX ATC 2010, section 2.1: a znode bound to the session that made it, removed when the session ends); etcd keys attached to a lease; across groups, CockroachDB's sqlliveness sessions, which rows in other ranges name and which make those rows void once the session is seen dead (from memory). | b: ZooKeeper's ephemeral nodes (a node carries its session's id and is deleted, through the log, when the session expires); etcd's leases with attached keys; across groups, CockroachDB's sqlliveness sessions (system.sqlliveness; holders elsewhere check the session and clean up its claims)
mechanisms.why: Added by both counters, blind (a's key: session-rows; b's key: presence-rows), with the same rows and the same precedent: ZooKeeper's ephemeral nodes and etcd's leases. mechanisms.name: Cluster version in #meta

mechanisms.state: In #meta's cluster record: the cluster version, that is the kernel and protocol version in force. Every frame carries its sender's protocol version.

mechanisms.model: Not modelled in this study.
mechanisms.source: DESIGN-V5 4.2 "Mixed versions" and the #meta record table (cluster: id, cluster version, ...)

mechanisms.name: Cluster credentials in #meta (CA envelopes, join tokens, certificates, the rotating secret)
mechanisms.option: every row with a metadata group
mechanisms.state: In #meta: the door secret, current and next; the CA key as envelopes encrypted to each #meta voter's key; single-use join tokens; each member's certificate; revoked certificates.
mechanisms.rules: A peer is let in only after it proves it holds the secret. The secret rotates through #meta as current and next, for a window in which both are valid. A join spends one join token and gets the member a certificate of its own. A removed member's certificate is revoked in #meta.
mechanisms.model: Not modelled in this study.
mechanisms.source: a: DESIGN-V5 4.5 "Identity and security" and the #meta record table; CLAUDE.md (kernel/door, V4-30) | b: DESIGN-V5 4.5 'Identity and security'; REQUIREMENTS OPS-14

From memory. | b: Docker swarm mode (its Raft store holds the cluster CA, the join tokens and the node certificates; `docker swarm join-token --rotate`, `docker swarm ca --rotate`); CockroachDB's join tokens (`cockroach node create-join-token`); kubeadm bootstrap tokens

Same state and rules in the same role as Swarm's. Not novel. | b: Missed by the list: named, replicated state with its own rules. Same state, same rules, same role as swarm mode. cited from memory, sure of the system and the mechanism.

mechanisms.name: Queue claims (leases and delivery counts on message rows)
mechanisms.option: every row that serves P-09 (the queue library, on the claim op)
mechanisms.state: Per message row of a queue: its claim's lease end and its delivery count. A dead-letter resource holds the rows past the limit.
mechanisms.rules: take(n) is one claim at the writer: the first n unclaimed rows, leased from writer time, with the count raised. An ack removes the row; a lapsed lease makes it claimable again; past the limit it moves to the dead-letter resource. A take hands over what it has at once (A-10).
mechanisms.model: Not modelled in this study (E-44 ran the pattern on JetStream).
mechanisms.source: DESIGN-V5 5.3 'Queue'; REQUIREMENTS P-09; AMENDMENTS A-10 (a take hands over what it has at once); E-44 (measured on JetStream: 294 jobs acked once, 6 dead-lettered)
mechanisms.precedent: Amazon SQS (a visibility timeout per received message, a receive count, a redrive to a dead-letter queue past maxReceiveCount); Redis Streams' pending entries with delivery counts (XCLAIM)
mechanisms.why: Added by b; taken, not novel: same state and rules as Amazon SQS (a visibility timeout and a receive count per message, a redrive to a dead-letter queue) and Redis Streams' pending entries. The list named the claim op only inside writer-judging; the lease and the count per message row are state of their own, as lock-rows' are. BUY is taken out: on JetStream the claim is JetStream's own ack wait and delivery count (E-44: a pull consumer whose ack wait is the lease), inside outside-log, as b itself judged for consumer groups. a did not list it.

mechanisms.name: Forks (a new resource that starts from the parent's snapshots)
mechanisms.option: every row with a metadata group (fero test, TEST-05 and TEST-06)
mechanisms.state: In #meta, per fork: a new resource whose groups start from named snapshots and segments of the parent's groups.
mechanisms.rules: A fork writes one #meta record per group and copies nothing. The parent may not drop a snapshot or a segment that a fork names.
mechanisms.model: Not modelled in this study (E-06 measured fork cost).
mechanisms.source: DESIGN-V5 6.2 (piece 8: 'a fork is a new resource whose shards start from the parent's shards' snapshots') and 4.1 ('no fork references it'); REQUIREMENTS TEST-05, TEST-06; E-06 (measured)

mechanisms.name: Recorder of kernel inputs
mechanisms.option: every row with a deterministic kernel of its own (OPS-11 d)
mechanisms.state: Per process: a recording of every kernel input (whole frames, ticks, disk and object-store completions), with bulk bytes named by journal reference.
mechanisms.rules: Every input is recorded before the kernel steps on it. The journal is kept for as long as the recorder's window refers to it. A dump replays byte for byte.
mechanisms.model: Not modelled; E-42 measured it (1.1 to 1.7 % of a core, 18 of 18 replays byte-identical).
mechanisms.source: REQUIREMENTS OPS-11 (d); AMENDMENTS A-09 (three recorder rules, counted there as format rules); E-42 (measured: 1.1 to 1.7 % of a core; BUY and V4 cannot have it)
mechanisms.precedent: Aeron Cluster with Aeron Archive (every input to the state machine is recorded in order and can be replayed); VoltDB's command logging (inputs logged, replayed deterministically); rr (record every nondeterministic input, replay exactly)
mechanisms.why: Added by b; taken, not novel (Aeron Archive with Aeron Cluster; VoltDB's command log; rr). A-09 counts the recorder's three rules as format rules. But the tape is a file on disk with a rule that writes it, and it holds the journal's retention, so by DEV-10 (a)'s letter it is a mechanism. Its list leaves out PD, ISR, SLOG and OBJ without saying they cannot, and each of them runs fero's own deterministic kernel (DEV-07), so they carry it too: 18 rows, not b's 14. a did not list it.

disagreements.what: novel or not
disagreements.why: Referee, with the source read. Same state: a slowness score per store, compared with the peers' mean, where the leader runs. Same rule: a leader whose own score passes a threshold and sits well above its peers' hands leadership away by itself. Same role: a slow leader in a cluster with no controller. Only the score's input differs (storage overload and disk health there; latency against the followers here). fero's rule was named, not written (A-03), so its form is still open, and REQUIREMENTS X17 asks for the published fix. So it settles as not novel on one condition: fero builds it in CockroachDB's form (an absolute threshold plus a margin over the peers' mean). b's doubt, that the feature is off by default, does not hold on the current source. By DEV-10 (a)'s letter it names no durable state; X17 asks to count it, so it stays in the file.

disagreements.what: novel or not
